Name: Something Easy
Description: New Taipei｜Something Easy GuesthouseA Window to Tranquility in a Mountain TownAs you ride up the mountain into the town of Jiufen, you catch sight of the misty mountains in the distance and see the sun pierce the clouds, warming the emerald-green mountainside. Disembarking from your ride, you recall the words of your host, Min, who warned that you would have to pass through the bustling old-street district on your way to the guesthouse. As you walk to the end of the street, you begin to foresee what is in store, as images of the elegant, tranquil face of Jiufen begin to fill your mind.A life of peace and quiet on the side of the mountainWalking along stone steps, you wind your way this way and that down the narrow alleys until you reach the appointed destination of Jiufen Elementary School, where you are met by the sweet smile of your host, Min. You follow her for less than three minutes until you reach the inconspicuous entrance of Something Easy Guesthouse to one side of the steep stone laneway. You close the door behind you and, slipping out of your shoes and into the slippers your host has prepared, you step onto the warm solid-wood floorboards. You bask in the warm lighting of the place, leaving the cold air of the mountains behind, as the mellow wooden environs instantly set your mind at ease.This space was originally designed to meet the vacation needs of Min’s family. From the verawood floorboards to the array of solid teakwood furniture, every corner of the space reveals her family’s insistence on quality and texture. The house, which is situated on the edge of this hillside town, affords you secluded, peaceful lodgings for your getaway from busy city life.Waking up free from worry in a scenic landscapeYou gently open the door to each of the rooms and walk in towards an entire wall of floor-to-ceiling windows. You gaze upon the mountain range beyond, the peaks extending layer upon layer all the way to the ocean where ocean and sky meet on the horizon. If you choose to stay in an upstairs room, you may enjoy the luxury of your own small living room, allowing you the freedom to laze about on the sofa in the company of the majestic landscape.As the evening sky gradually darkens, the lights of the town illuminate the mountainside one by one. Min has thoughtfully equipped your bathroom with a heater / dehumidifier so that you may stay warm and dry at all times. After you’ve enjoyed a lavish bath, connect to the room’s bluetooth sound system to play your favorite tunes. Finally, lie down on the large double bed and slowly drift into slumberland.A calm corner on the Old StreetAs morning breaks and the gentle sunlight peeks through the cracks of the curtains, you unhurriedly awake to meet the day. The single-serving coffee maker brews a silky smooth latte for you to enjoy on the rooftop patio with a few slices of toast and jam. In contrast to yesterday evening’s misty mountain scenery, the daytime skies in Jiufen appear especially clear and bright - the turquoise blue of the ocean blending into the azure blue of the sky. Glancing downwards, you realize the bustle of Jiufen Old Street is right below your feet. Anticipation of perusing the old street at a leisurely pace begins to build, as you imagine the undiscovered pleasures awaiting you within.Something Easy Guesthouse is situated in a corner of Jiufen’s bustling Old Street, inviting you to settle into your own tranquil corner from which to peacefully observe the everyday life of this hillside town. Regardless of the countless tumultuous days of your life, all that is left now is a wall of windows and the serene landscape beyond. From here, discover the peaceful getaway of your dreams.

Description: Fish Fun is situated next to Hualien City Office. Everything needed for convenient living is easily available . As for good food in Hualien: There are the Sankokuighi Drink & Foods Restaurant, Yue Lu (Moon House), Ying Tien Yeh, Health and Wellness House, Hua Ben House (Kagawa), Lichuan Fish Pond, Shuen Fu Yu Snack Stand, Gong Cheng Steamed Buns, Mr. Goose Meat, Lai Cheng Pork Chop, China Noodle Shop, First Barbecue Shop, Chiang Family Hualien Style Coffin Boards, all serving up delicious delicacies at a reasonable price. I like fishing. In Hualien, I have been in the fishing equipment business for over 20 years. I inherited the 40 year old store from my father. I love fishing, and often go rock fishing, beach fishing, and boat fishing on the river or the sea, enjoying the fresh air of Mother Nature and cool sea breeze. Hualien is a beautiful place.

Description: Taipei’s prestigious Japanese-style hotel, the Okura Prestige Taipei, is located in the downtown part of the city in the Nanjing East and Zhongshan North Road Commercial Area, whose history dates back to the Japanese colonial era, when it was a gathering place for merchants. The building’s design was the newest creation of famous Hong Kong designer Rocco Design Architects Limited, and its decoration was directed by Chhada, Siembieda & Associates Ltd, a famous hotel design company from Hong Kong. The main hall features a modern classical European design. Classic European patterns and crystal lighting are thoughtfully placed within the simple colors and line of the modern space, producing a low-key yet calm atmosphere. The space features traditional Japanese elegant design, balancing function and aesthetics and converying the Japanese cultural ideal of harmony with nature. In the relaxed, comfortable space, one can experience Tokyo’s friendly and harmonious spirit of service, continuing a half-century legacy of attentive customer service. Featuring a luxurious living experience and rich living entertainment and style, the hotel’s 208 modern rooms and suites come with a raised space design that perfectly combines modern classical decoration and Japanese functional aesthetics to provide visitors with the ultimate quiet and comfortable accommodation. We also provide a professional gym, heated rooftop pool, spa, and sauna, where you can relax your body and mind. The hotel also includes a multi-purpose meeting area serviced by attentive staff ready to meet your needs. Customized banquet and professional meeting planning makes this a perfect place to hold important banquets and meetings. Feast on fine food and beverages rivaling Tokyo –YAMAZATO fine Japanese Cuisine, Toh-Ka-Lin Chinese Restaurant, and other representative Japanese restaurants have made their home in Okura Prestige Taipei, where you can enjoy classic Japanese cuisine. The hotel also includes the European-style Continental Room, featuring an all-day buffet, The Nine Bakery, and The Pearl, a great bar to relax in and sip fine brews from around the world. The heated rooftop pool features another bar with magnificent views of Taipei 101, the cityscape, and surrounding mountains.

Description: Penghu｜Murraya Paniculata VillaA classical Fujian-style vacation home beside the waterDriving along County Road 201, you see none of the hustle and bustle of Penghu City, as the spacious scenery along the sides of the road comes alive. You begin to hum a little country ditty, as you drive towards the classically appealing style of Murraya Paniculata Villa which sits at the end of the lane as if awaiting your arrival.Go to bed in secluded relaxation, surrounded by exquisite brick and tileThe gorgeous courtyard entrance to Murraya Paniculata Villa employs orange brick as its basic style while brightly colored ceramic tiles frame the two characters of the Chinese name to extend a magnificent welcome to all visiting travelers. A refreshing breeze blows by as you enter the premises and see several lotus blossoms are just waiting to burst into bloom in the pool out in front of the house. You raise your head and look upwards beneath the saddle-shaped Fujian-style roof ridge to see elaborate, vivid paintings of birds and flowers frolicking as if about to leap out at you. Upon closer inspection you realize that the scene is made by the nearly-lost traditional art of Taiwanese ceramic applique! Guesthouse owner, Well, especially sought out a team of old-house restoration specialists who carried out their renovation of the entire structure using ancient construction methods. Using the coral stone material unique to Penghu, the old building was made new so that visiting travelers might also enjoy the beauty of an ancient homestead.As the clear yellow sun creeps over the rooftop of Murraya Paniculata Villa, each square inch appears, under the brilliant sunlight, as if sprinkled with gold leaf. In the afterglow of sunset, and in the lamplight after darkness falls, numerous yellow lights appear like ornaments under the violet night sky. Light and shadow move with the passing of time, and the homestead’s winsome reflection is inverted in the waters of the pool. The picturesque reflection appears as if anew at progressive moments throughout the day, at once imposing and beautiful, yet refined and tranquil. Ancient but not old-fashioned, elegant yet adaptiveBehind the simple entrance, however, you’ll be surprised to find your own personal swimming pool! Inside the ancient homestead, you can enjoy all the modern comforts, and allow the light-reflecting water to mirror all the happiness of your vacation. As you push open the gold-leaf painted wooden shutter doors, you behold the elegant furniture in classical Chinese-style. Whether it is the “imperial tutor’s chair”, the old food cabinet, or the wooden linen dresser, each and every implement is refined and unique.When the moment comes to rest and light penetrates outward from the holes in driftwood lamp shades, you make yourself a refreshing cup of Hsiang-ju teasane, a local specialty, and once more wash the dust away with a handful of water from the ceramic lotus flower sink. You savor the remaining light of the sunset which slides down the roof ridge in preparation to embrace the moon in a sound slumber. Enjoy your own meditative purelandOpening the doors in the morning, the brightly smiling housekeeper delivers a diverse breakfast: plump, round meatballs, crisp fried dumplings, tasty iced black tea, and the local favorite of Zhongji baked sesame seed-coated cakes, with a refreshing fruit sandwich to finish the meal. The sumptuous food is deeply satisfying, like a classical nanguan musical performance; sometimes singing, sometimes playing a tune, each delivering its own clever magic whilst making harmonious music together.You push open the front gate and leave Murraya Paniculata Villa, with the dazzling noonhour sun shining on the water of the pool. You approach the surface of the water and discover the lotus flower has bloomed, while little tilapia fish dart between the lotus leaves, their charming silhouettes dancing on the surface of the water. You secretly store this amiable scene deep in your heart, as if, now, you and Penghu share a beautiful secret.

Name: BLACK TEA WORKSHOP
Description: One day, a child raised beneath the black tea tree decided to leave the workplace behind and return to a place of serene mountains and the scenic countryside, his pure spiritual and life hometown, in order to live with the black tea plants and help the garden that raised him continue to grow sustainably. When the two children put aside their work and decide to help their parents, Black Tea Workshop was born! United in heart and mind, the family entered the world of black tea one step at a time. In order to realize their dream, they started with the designs, and following much debate, decided on a Tudor architectural style – simple, natural, refined, and down-to-earth. They drew up several designs matching the scale of their ideas for lattice windows which let in sunlight and greenery while providing great views. After cutting, pasting, and comparing, they decided on an ideal rectangular 4:3 ratio, changing the deep, narrow Tudor windows into a larger, wider design. For the color coordination of the building’s exterior, they not only diligently searched the Internet to select roof tiles, colors, magnets, tiles, and wood floors, but also visited manufacturers around Taichung to compare and contrast until they found the right texture and patterns. The bed and breakfast’s rooms are named based on the theme of black tea, such as Black Tea Seed, Black Tea Ren, Workshop Aged Tea, and Taiwanese Tea No. 18. The rooms also feature different-themed decoration, with the characters or pictures created by the workshop family or photographs subjected to a special pressure proces, giving them a unique, original style. In order to help guests feel at home, black tea pillows are provided, filling the room with a faint fragrance. The pillows are made by the three generations of family members who run the business and have been personally involved in everything from producing tea to sewing pillows. In addition to the fragrance of the pillows, the room walkways feature pictures detailing the process of hard work that goes into making pillows. In keeping with the black tea theme, room lights are designed with black tea leaves, and under the contrast of the soft light, the leaves spread out, contributing to Black Tea Workshop’s unique style. Rooms are spacious and well-lit inside and out, simple and refined in layout, and faintly fragrant of black tea – features provided by the Black Tea Workshop family in order to provide honored guests with the best and most comfortable atmosphere. The main goal of the workshop is sustainable management of the old tea garden, which naturally makes the old trees the point of focus. So before the 2010 Chinese New Year, in the dead of winter which is the best time for transplanting, the old trees are moved from the garden inside the house to be taken care of. We currently grow them in the Black Tea Workshop courtyard, where they accompany us each day. The days pass just as they once did amidst the tea trees; even when we don’t go to the garden anymore, we feel their presence. When you come to Black Tea Workshop, please take a close look at them. These are the trees that raised our family, standing strong and tall, braving winds and rain for over sixty years! Black Tea Workshop also features cuisine made from old tea garden black tea and seasonal fruits and vegetables. Our specialty milk tea blends the fragrance of milk and tea, refreshing without being overly sweet, and goes well with our handmade cookies and black tea cheesecake. Black Tea Workshop is a place that will leave wonderful memories! This is Black Tea Workshop! A small, warm, beautiful, carefree place!

Name: Mei Shiou B&B
Description: Yilan｜Meishiou B&B A Fairytale-Like Carpenter’s HouseWhite clouds drift through the clear, blue Yilan skies as you sing a song and stroll along the country lanes. Suddenly, you hear the energetic barking of a little dog. A little black and white Chihuahua stares at you with its sparkling big eyes. Behind it, a three-level building painted in off-white and brown comes into view. Welcome to Meishiou B&B!Countryside memoirs of a happy encounter with woodPushing open the low, wooden gate, you enter a garden filled with lush and vibrant flowers and plants. Red dragonflies accompany you down the crushed stone pathway right up to the front door. On the veranda, you find a sturdy wooden shoe cabinet above which a blackboard has been colorfully decorated with the words “Meishiou B&B: lodging, woodworking, playful life.” You open the door to a room full of richly colored wooden furniture, giving the interior the feeling of a small forest. Lifting your head, you see a beautiful scene of blue sky and green trees out the window, and you feel as if you’ve entered the home of a fairytale elf!This fairytale-like home and all the beautiful furniture within is a product of the hard work of your hosts. The doghouse in the entrance is your hostess Meishiou’s first woodworking project, to create a warm little corner for her beloved dog, Bogi. She has since transformed herself into a stylish female carpenter! She dragged Piety, who loves DIY projects, into her plan, to become her number-one helper. Piety’s passion for carpentry, however, originates from his inherent desire to get his hands on everything around him. He once even helped SGS to do inspection work! Eventually, they built a tiny woodworking shop behind their house, helping to establish their dream home. A cozy, warm woodworking shop, a miniature tri-color fairytaleGoing up stairs, you see Meishiou’s creativity in the natural tri-color decor: red, blue, and green. Each room seems to embody its own miniature fairytale. The first page of the tale tells the story of a sunflower growing up in a safflower garden. With multi-colored pillows and tender-colored walls, the “Red Warmth Room” is a little paradise just for you and your furry friend, set up to give you the most delightful experience before settling in for bed.The second page of the tale tells of an elf’s fantasy adventure in the green forest. The “Green Forest Room” is the only four-person room at Meishiou B&B, serving as the perfect secret base for you and your friends to share a vacation together. A red dinosaur dangling from a floating balloon drifts up near the ceiling, the clock on his belly tick-tocking away as if to suggest that this is the moment for a joyous adventure to begin!On the third floor, you open the third page of the tale, where a mermaid princess shares her story about the world beneath the sea. The “Blue Waters Room” has an elevated wooden floor with a row of tall blue waves for bed headboards. This room has the only bathtub, and it’s pink, like a romantic blessing from the mermaid princess.A fairytale home converging with real lifeIn the morning, you walk out onto the balcony, take a deep breath of that fresh, clean Yilan air, and catch a whiff of a delicious breakfast cooking! Soy milk, a fresh fruit and vegetable salad, mashed potato balls, soft-boiled eggs, and perfectly toasted bread combine for a simple yet perfectly energizing breakfast. If you’re intrigued by Meishiou and Piety’s woodworking life, you can book a seat in Friday’s woodworking course for a chance to hammer around with Meishiou in the workshop! Different than your standard carpentry course, Meishiou enjoys using love to create woodcrafts with her guests. Piety humorously refers to their workshop as their “delivery room” where you can experience with your own hands the satisfaction of creating things from wood.The warm feeling inside the house is just like the interaction between Meishiou and Piety – comfortable and cozy. When they met each other, one had just completed a job, while the other had fallen in love with hiking as a way of coping with a break up. They began hiking, fishing, and bicycle-riding together - they’ve even conquered half of the hundred highest peaks in Taiwan. Having an unspoken understanding of one another, they began to construct their guesthouse together. They’ve been through a lot in their countryside life; even though Piety recently fell seriously ill, the illness was unable to defeat them as they faced it with unyielding optimism. Description: New Shui Diao Ge Tou B&B  Traditional-Style Taiwanese Building is a large traditional residence featuring a traditional layout, “11 Support” style structure with 11 pillars, and front and rear sections connected on the left and right sides. It was built by Huang Sunzhang around the turn of the 20th century. The Kinmen National Parks of Taiwan had the land rights for 30 years and renovated the building before turning it over to be privately operated as a B&B. New Shui Diao Ge Tou Bed & Breakfast took its name from a famous poem by Su Dongpo as well as its location by the water. It has 7 rooms; 4 of the rooms have upper attics and can accommodate 2-4 people, while the 3 rooms on the right side are doubles which can accommodate 14-22 people. The overall design combines traditional building features with bright, clean modern suite rooms, making this a warm, comfortable B&B. Here you can experience the wisdom and charming layout of Kinmen’s old buildings, as well as a sense of spiritual fulfillment. These old buildings have a long and colorful history; the weathered stone slabs have stood firm against the test of time and the mottled red bricks and tiles still shine after a long rain. Life is to be celebrated and cherished! Share a moment of peace and quiet with family and friends, and hold it as a beautiful, lasting memory – this is the sublime power of our traditional-style B&B. Description: Introduction of Ji-Yue VillaJiu-Zhou Lake is a quiet and secluded mountain settlement, and later the Agriculture Committee has promoted the "Rich Countryside" project, and developed the mountain settlement into a combination of agriculture and tourism leisure area. The original environment is a beautiful mountain and river condition, and has been improved with recreational facilities of trails, pavilions and landscape table. The local farmers have set up sightseeing orchards and Hakka restaurants. With these preparation, Jiu-Zhou Lake is expected to become a popular leisure area.  There are three hiking trails in the Jiu-Zhou Lake area, namely, "Jiu-fu", "Guan- Nan" and "Ji-Yue". Hiking trails can be found in the mountain and the lake area. Three trails have been planned with stone steps, red brick, or sleepers. The trails are also wide and safe to walk freely. People can absorb the natural phytoncide for about two hours while walking these three trails among the old acacia trees, suitable leisure trails for young and old people as well as children.   "Ji-Yue Villa" becomes famous because it is close to Ji-Yue trail. People can come to Ji-Yue Villa from Ji-shan Bridge of Jiu-fu road along the river with bald pines planted by the Soil and Water Conservation Bureau. The bald pines have different color in four different seasons. The scenery is especially beautiful in the winter like the northland style bleak landscape. The residence also retains the traditional Hakka red brick house, part of the villa is currently open for the accommodation and resting place of tourists. Allegedly, the children of the original house owner are very smart with good school grades. Currently, they are very successful in the education sector and hold high work positions in the academia circle. This house is built facing the mountain with river and backing mountain geographical location, the so called good Feng-Shui pattern " Jade Belt Waist ", and this house is also called "Champion Home" by the local people. This house retains the ancient hakka kitchen stove that worships the traditional Chinese gods called "Stove God". When visitors arrive at the "Ancient House", they are greeted with a row of red brick and tile-roofed house. Walking red brick on the floor, the visitors will experience the sense of the past. Under the hundred-year lychee tree in the courtyard, tourists can rest and chat. In the manor, there are several old camphor trees that are extremely large and precious old trees.The green grass is planted in the garden and there is a "Big Fish" in the form of a fish pond, where the carps swim in fish pond and the wood flooring platform is the best view of the beautiful scenery and the bald pines. It is also possible to gaze at “South Park”from the manor, a good recreational activity venue for the group tourists to dance and sing songs. It is like a paradise and it is  also a wonderful choice for vacation and relaxation.Service Items:1. Accommodation2. Mountaineering Trip Planning (Itinerary Tour)3. Name: Albe Farm Homestay
Description: Aliban Ecological Farm is located in the Shimen District of New Taipei City, on a beautiful 10-plus-hectare valley around 130 meters above sea level. Only a couple of buildings sit on this exapnsive area, all of which are repurposed former farmhouses, now being used as guest accommodation or activity spaces. Aliban is a perfect place for nature lovers, boasting dense old-growth forest, broad grasslands and aquatic habitats, which leaves the air filled with the sounds of birds and frogs. The environment here is diverse in wildlife, with over 100 species of butterfly, over 70 species of birds, 19 species of frogs, and over 60 species of dragonfly. During the summer, you’ll find butterflies, dragonflies, cicadas, and beetles in the daytime and fireflies, frogs (including the endangered Rana taipehensis), and even recently molted cicadas at night. Aliban Ecological Farm is also active in education, not only providing professional guided tours, but also planning healthy, interesting, and educational outdoor activities, making it a great place for school trips. It also provides food, drinks, and accommodation, with delicious homemade food using local ingredients, including Shimen tea, black boar meat from Sanzhi, free-range chicken, and fresh seafood and vegetables. At the outdoor café, you can experience both the beauty of the mountain scenery and the wonderful fragrance of the coffee. Aliban offers a relaxing, clean, and comfortable accommodation experience, and hopes that through your stay, you’ll get to better understand and treasure nature!

Description: Hualien｜Bears in the Forest GuesthouseBears! A Comfortable Vacation on the LakesideYour car drives into Shoufeng township, situated in Hualien county between the central and coastal mountain ranges. Hidden away down laneways and between farmers’ fields you discover Yun Shan Shui Park. Across a bridge, several small white cottages rest between white clouds, green hills, and crystal-clear waters. Bears in the Forest Guesthouse invites you to enter a verdant landscape on the side of a lake, to enjoy a comfortable vacation… with bears and the forest!Bears will enjoy your vacation with youThe wind blows across a vast field of grass spread out like a green carpet. A big bear doll stands in the doorway outfitted like a British guard to welcome you. Pushing open the wooden doors, bear dolls one after another are to be found throughout the lobby. Coming here is all about relaxing with the bears!Happy music begins to play while the large glass windows reflect the lake and the emerald green scenery beyond. You only need to slow your pace, and breathe deep the fresh clean air. Look up from the grassy lawn at the starry night sky with the natural symphony of bird and insect song surrounding you.A dreamland by the lakesideAllen, the host of Bears in the Forest Guesthouse, recalls of when he came to Hualien to serve in the military. He was attracted to the great mountains and waters, and to the good air. At that time, he established his goal to return to this place and build a comfortable little house. He planned the gardens in European style and designed the rooms with Japanese elements. Allen has help from friends with business and marketing experience. He also has ties with the locals, and his diligent efforts bring people the same satisfaction and contentment as entering the forest.The Guesthouse is made up of 12 independent little houses in five different styles, such as four-person rooms suitable for bringing your parents or your children to enjoy together. Couples or pairs, on the other hand, might choose to check into a loft or an exquisite little double room. There is a little black teddy bear friend in every room, or several cute, loveable bear dolls lying on the sofa. Every washroom has a heating system and the pleasant smell of Chinese juniper. Enjoying your own private courtyard in the dim evening light, you feel inspired to soak in the outdoor hot spring and wash away your exhaustion. Local Hualien vegetables in your mealsThe moment you check in, cute bear cookies are laid on the table before you, paired with panna cotta, Hualien sweet potato cakes, and a variety of other local snacks. You can also book in advance for a chef’s tasting menu to enjoy delicious dishes made with local ingredients. In the morning, you cross the spacious lawn on your way to the lobby to enjoy a sumptuous Taiwanese style breakfast consisting of cold-dressed lotus root, salted egg with wild bitter gourd, beef and potato stew, and sauteed salmon accompanied by a bowl of sweet potato congee for a beautiful start to the day. You set out into the breeze on a reserved bicycle to admire the deep green scenery and tranquil atmosphere of the lake. At Bears in the Forest Guesthouse, you’ll feel the warmth of the bear’s embrace.

Description: Fu Ren Bed & Breakfast is a stone building nearly 80 years old. On October 15, 2003, the owner bought a NT$20 sickle and cut a basket-size bundle of grass by the stairs in front of the building. Thick wild grass and many large trees obstructed views of the building and prevented such this great construction project from being completed. So he called home and told his parents about the situation, asking them to come to Matsu and help renovate the old structure. It was very hard work, but his parents showed their love by helping and supporting him through the entire process. We would like to thank many people for making this possible. The building’s beauty is really unbelievable, and there is not a single nail to be found in the internal wood structure. The building is also well-situated, facing Fu-Ao Wharf, from where one can see little white boats traveling between the islands during the day and the most beautiful sights in the evening, including the moon in the middle of the month. Flowers of all colors make their appearances by season, butterflies dance in the wind, and carefree birds fly overhead. Spring brings romance, summer passion, autumn beauty, and winter serenity, and the beauty of it all touches the heart! We’ve prepared a lucky key to open the door to your emotions. Stay in a traditional stone house, embrace the ocean, and enjoy the sunrise in the morning and waves during the day. The sea is right at your doorstep! Description: Dreaming of life on the Farm? Many people may fantasize about living in the country, but only a very few ever get around to living the pastoral life a reality.Chuo Chen Ming had her epiphany 30 years ago on the eve of her 40th birthday. “If I don’t begin working on my dreams while my mind and body are at their peak,” she thought, “when am I going to do it?” Soon after, she was crossing hill and dale with a real estate agent haunting for the perfect place. When she found it at the mountains of Kengfeng village at Toucheng Township, Yilan County, she spent all of the more than NT$5 million she had earned from her garment factory and teaching, to buy it. Thus begun what was to become the legendary story of the farming Grandma. “Look, children!” exclaims Chuo Chen Ming, “That’s our national bird, the Formosa blue magpie. They’re very family-oriented birds. After the chicks grow up, they help their parents raise their younger siblings”. She then leans forward to make sure she doesn’t miss any of the questions coming from the large group of children before her.Her eyes and ears are surprisingly sharp in spite of her 68 years- there’s no movement in the forest that escape her notice. Visitors to the Toucheng Leisure Farm in Yilan County, all remember the grandmotherly old woman who pops up in the Farm. Always bursting with energy, she is happy to share her opinions with visitors, including her insistence that the farm grow its food organically, and prepare it in a traditional fashion. Her personality is so warm and frank that visitors almost always end up addressing as “Mama Chuo” regardless of their own age. Chuo Chen Ming was born in Chingshui Township, Taichung County, Taiwan in 1940. After graduating from The Taipei Women’s Normal College, (now the Taipei Municipal University of Education), she began working as a teacher primarily of sixth graders.

Name: Monetgarden Coffee Grange(B&B)
Description: ★Monet Garden—Don Gus Coffee Farm is the main agency for the renowned Balanjoyo Coffee. With top quality coffee beans imported directly from the volcano district in Guademala, Mr. Chang as the farm owner brews limited amount daily. Therefore, the entire farm manifests mysterious atmosphere integrating Latino romance and Mayan magic. The setting of Central American Tropical Forest is decorated with numerous artifacts from Mayan ruins. Even furniture is handmade by Mayan workers, while bed cover is made from the most famous Mayan textile.   ★Such a unique style combining Latino romance and Mayan magic can only be represented via techniques of the impressionist school. Mr. Chang and his son who majored in architecture present natural simplicity with joint efforts so that aesthetic elegance is distributed via impressionist approach. Of course, a water lily pond is established here to elicit reminiscence of the famous painting by Claude Monet. Our farm is named as Monet Garden for this reason.  ★The farm has rich natural ecosystems. Visitors inadvertently encounter a variety of lizards, stag beetles, and rhinoceros beetles here. Dragonflies, butterflies, Gunder brown frogs come back every spring and summer. In front of the Mayan Suite, there is a waterway, derived from the mountain creek, zigzagging into the water lily pond. Five generations of kois and Chinese sturgeons live in the water lily pond along with many other fishes from mountain creeks riding currents down here as passers-by.   The geese couple, Pipi and Yaya, are the most welcome ambassadors of goodwill. They greet people with passion. Another pair of Japanese rooster and hen stroll leisurely to seek feed. With the advent of night, you can sit on the stairway of the Monet Chicken Farm to appreciate the scene with bird species flying on top of the trees to rest in sleep.  ★Located to the north end of East Rift Valley, Carp Like has abundant picturesque natural ecosystems. From March to May every year, tourists flock here to view fireflies. ★A five-kilometer trip around the lake by bike or on foot is full of joy. So is sitting in the pagoda next to the lake with your heart and mind totally relaxed. Swinging on the lake by peddling a boat or shaking a canoe is fun as well. Scenic Spots Nearby:★White Abalone River and Gems Canyon----You can explore in stream-tracing, wade into the clear water, pick up gems, or follow the forest trail all the way to the Woods of Green Light in quest of natural ecosystems. ★Mukumugi Ecological Garden----It is Toroko Gorge in miniature. As you wade into the creeks, schools of shoveljaw carps will play with you by licking your soles. ★South Lake Forest Park----Formerly Harlem Forest with papaya trees all over, the Park now has an exhibition hall as well as an ecological classroom. The mini-rail which used to distribute logs has long discontinued. Strolling among the remaining rail tracks, you will be surrounded by chirping birds and fragrant flowers as Carp Lake mirrors your reflection. ★Carp Hill Hiking Trail----Stepping on the observatory six-hundred kilometers in height, you can view Mount Chilai in the north from afar. Winter will decorate the hilltop with snow. And the blue Pacific is visible at the east side.  ★From Monet Garden to downtown Hualien is an easy ride of approximately twenty minutes. All the main scenic areas are within half-hour ride by car.

After thinking carefully, he settled down in Hualien - the most beautiful area in Taiwan. He spent two years completing his own buildings- from design and plan to selecting materials and constructing, and he gradually completed the perfect B&B in his mind. He owned two buildings for the B&B. Building A, with dark red brick walls, vintage electric fans, obvious pipelines and log doors, makes you go back to the 1950s. Building B, with black iron partition cabinet, leather sofa and glossy floor, shows an ornate style to make you feel like displaced in time and place. There is no special B&B like Ji Ye Jing Zhan Villa Homestay in Taiwan. Description: Miaoli｜House of Tung FlowersWhite snow in a mountain forest; the delight of Tung flower landFollowing Provincial Highway Six up into the mountains, you breathe the sweet, clear air of Miaoli County. Turning down a winding mountain road, you see a flurry of snow-like Tung flowers - the so-called May Snows. Trees encompass the road from both sides as you approach your beautiful mountain destination - House of Tung Flowers. Between the elegance of nature and the deliciousness of exquisitely prepared meals, you savor the taste of happiness.Afternoon tea in the mountains beneath the Tung treesThe layered green landscape of House of Tung Flowers unfolds before your eyes, with a lofty tung tree standing directly in the middle of the gardens, quietly extending its branches to bathe in the warm sunlight. You set out across a wooden pathway strewn with Tung flowers and resembling snow-covered ground, and stroll between the Tung, Phoebe zhennan, umbrella, and camellia assamica trees. The mountain breeze rustles the tree leaves as the sounds of insects and birds enters your ears, uniting into a lively forest concerto.In the afternoon, you enter the glass-walled tea room, with light spilling in from all sides. To one side sits a dessert cabinet full of sweets from the famous RT Bakery House. Have as much as you like, along with hot tea and coffee. Seated indoors or out, the scenery is beautiful any season of the year, not just during the Tung flower season. In spring, fresh emerald-green leaves sprout all around. In summer, the tung trees produce a snow of white flowers. In autumn, the maples shine red in the forest. And in winter, the mountain forests are shrouded in clouds and mist.Resting between fragrant trees, taste a creative, menu-free Hakka-style mealStepping into the three-story building, the scent of Chinese fir filling the entire space relieves your exhausted mind. At House of Tung Flowers, the furnishings in each room are made of solid wood, accentuated with exquisite antique lamps, and include a capsule coffee machine and complementary RT Bakery House cookies. The interior design includes Japanese tatami mats as well as wooden rocking chairs, with large windows that afford beautiful views of the mountain forests. You can sit on the balcony and breathe phytoncides from the comfort of hanging chairs, or soak in the bathtub to completely relax. With a maximum capacity of 20 people, House of Tung Flowers is well-suited for a family or a group of friends to reserve the entire wooden structure. With karaoke in the first floor common room and a small living room on the third floor where family and friends can play chess or chat with each other.A one night stay includes three meals, yet the thing most anticipated by visitors to House of Tung Flowers is the menu-free fusion dinner incorporating local ingredients and traditional Hakka flavors. Red date vinegar is used to start the meal off, followed by lotus root wrapped in the sweetness of Hakka-style grass jelly made of Chinese mesona. A bamboo steamer full of fresh seasonal vegetables with homemade kumquat sauce satisfies all the senses. A uniquely flavored bean curd chicken soup, served with crisp bread stuffed with Italian rice-flour noodles emits distinct Italian aroma. The sweet fish imparts the fresh sweetness of the sea, while the broiled Japanese beef (wagyu) simply cannot be missed. Finally, enjoy a bite of delicate almond tofu and a glass from host James’s private wine collection to bring your beautiful evening to a close. In contrast with one’s impression of the usual fixed villa menu, the food at House of Tung Flowers employs meticulous western-style techniques and the ingenious fusion of Hakka cuisine and Taiwanese ingredients to bring to each traveler an elegant and refined dining experience. James - promoting Taiwan’s tung flower season for the appreciation of the entire worldIn the morning, the mountain breeze urges you toward the breakfast table, where yet another sumptuous meal is laid out. Many summers ago, James decided to open his family home up to the public, to share the beautiful scenery with travelers by opening a guesthouse. The Hakka Affairs Council seized the opportunity to promote the Hakka tung flower season to attract large quantities of tourists, during which time House of Tung Flowers operates at full capacity every single day. Today, James has a full head of gray hair, yet in those first days, he truly was a pioneer, leading the way in the tung flower tourist market. With his endless Hakka passion and hospitality, he has been a great advocate of tung flower tourism during the month of May. Who would guess that he grew up in the Ximending neighborhood in Taipei! Yet he had always hoped to one day live in the tranquility of nature. Upon entering society, he continued his father’s construction business. At the turn of the millennium, in a time when many people could not even recognize a tung tree, he had come to admire the largest tung tree in Taiwan, right here beside House of Tung Flowers. He built his guesthouse and launched his one night, three meals slow living holiday package so that travelers can live in the mountains, and enjoy the tung flowers and delicious food. “Taiwan has many qualifications which surpass those of other countries, so we need to look at things from a new perspective, drawing in a tide of tourists from abroad, in order for Taiwan to build confidence!” With his warmth and sincerity, James invites travelers from around the world to come to this tranquil forest, to enjoy the tung flowers fluttering on the May breeze, like beautiful snow swirling in the air, and savor the taste of a truly happy vacation.

Description: Enjoy the relaxation and serenity of a harbor community and experience the limitless fun of a fishing village. Dongshih (Dongshi), the “township of three colors,” is a mixture of green, blue, and gray viewed from a distance and includes eight unique scenic sites and eight natural ecological sites, while the authentic seaside community provides a diverse travel experience. Try out the plump and crispy sweet Dongshih oysters, be a part of the Dongshih fish market, bustling with the sounds of vendors, and visit the Aogu wetland, Waisanding Sand Bar, the natural ecology display center…fully experience the unending charm of this little seaside community. Chuanzaitou Homestay located in Chuanzaitou, Dongshih Township, Chiayi County, was the first legally certified bed and breakfast in Chiayi. Located on the border between Dongshih Township, Puzih (Puzi) City, and Lioujiao (Liujiao) Township, Chuanzaitou was a place of beautiful childhood memories for Mr. Cai Zhencheng, the owner of the bed and breakfast. In order to introduce others to the beauty of this place, he and his wife returned to his hometown and established Chuanzaitou Homestay, promoting an outstanding in-depth cultural trip with package activities such as the Puzih Stream Levee Bike Trail and dragon boat rowing so that travelers may not only relax but thoroughly experience the carefree fun of the fields and fishing village. In addition to providing an outstanding, in-depth experience, Chuanzaitou offers a well-designed, warm, elegant, comfortable, bright, and secure resting place. During the day, take a in-depth tour of village experiences, such as the mangrove ecological area, Dongshih fishing wharf, and an ox-cart ride around the village, then spend the night at Chuanzaitou Homestay enjoying the peaceful countryside scenery and traditional three-section building compound and listening to the crickets. Bring the whole family!

Name: Wusulin Before
Description: Taoyuan｜Before B&BThe intoxicating delight of lingering between booksIn open fields only an hour south of Taipei sits a small villa, which brings together books and fine beer. Sitting brightly under a blue sky, the amber colored building of Before B&B invites you to join in writing the story of your unrestrained journey.Sipping beer with your nose in a bookAs you enter Before B&B, sunlight streams through large windows and spills across the square pattern of the terrazzo floors. The uneven wooden bookshelves along both walls give the sensation of being in a forest where the trees have grown to varying heights. In this staggered forest, the treasures hiding between the trees are not birds’ nests, but rather the book collection of B&B host Danny, as well as his collection of craft beer! According to Danny, books are like friends who enrich our innermost selves, while beer is a good companion for pleasant worldly conversation. These two items appear to be unrelated, yet they are Danny’s indispensable life companions. So the first floor of Danny’s B&B is an independent bookstore that sells beer. This design is not for profit, but rather to satisfy Danny’s heartfelt desire for sharing his passions with others. “My B&B is a part of my life. It is an extension of me, so you have to appreciate my lifestyle to stay in my B&B.” Danny comes across as somewhat arrogant and proud, but after all, confidence comes from working hard at what you do. The moment his family decided to refurbish their aged courtyard home, the opportunity to create Before B&B was born. Black Forest is the name of the area were Before B&B is situated, while Before is actually a play on “b-four”, as in bed, breakfast, books, and beer - all delightful things which Danny just can’t wait to share with travelling guests. You may buy a book with which it was love at first sight, or perhaps a bottle of mouthwatering beer to pass a relaxing afternoon.Volume after volume recounting the collage of lifeHeading upstairs past walls lined with books, you discover that Before B&B is itself a colorful hardcover storybook, each page containing different scenery, as the names of the five guest rooms imply. Occasionally flipping this storybook open to the “life style” page, the central mountain range, however distant, appears right before your eyes. Occasionally opening it up to the “fiction & literature” section or the pages describing “indigenous literature” and light streams in through skylights, illuminating the split-level loft design of the B&B. Meanwhile, you share your discoveries with friends in the nooks beneath the stairs. The page of this B&B storybook about “travel & food” is the tender green color of a grassy field, the warmth of the sun and the specs of pink flowers accompany you in welcoming springtime. Meanwhile in the gosling-yellow story regarding “kids’ picture books” you and your friends have ample room to roll freely around like children on the two large double beds. Yet no matter which meticulously collaged page you open the Before B&B storybook to, it is sure to bring your imagined scenery to life.Discover story after brilliant storyStanding there in a simple t-shirt with a bottle of beer in hand, Danny looks just like the character Ling Hu-chong out of Jin Yong’s famous 1967 martial arts novel “Swordsman” who regarded the liquor in his cup as a lifelong friend. Most surprising, though, is that the practice to which he has devoted more than twenty years of his life is not what is in his cup, but rather what lies between the pages of his books! With a laugh, Danny proclaims, “Not a day goes by that I don’t read a book, nor a day when I don’t drink alcohol.” Danny exudes an open and generous humor, and is quite insistent on realizing the ideals he feels passionate about. Though it isn’t easy to operate a bookstore, he still hopes to use the magic of his shop to help people fall in love with reading. Even when work keeps him busy, whenever he meets a like-minded traveler, he’s more than willing to discuss books over bottles of beer all night long. Danny appreciates life and is apt to follow his whims, just like that free and easy character Ling Hu-chong, laughing his way through life.When you arrive at Before B&B, please remember to leave your hurried urban pace at the door, take the time to truly enjoy a good book, a bottle of beer, or an amusing phrase from your amiable host, Danny. Shouldn’t everyone’s life contain just this kind of carefree comfort? On this trip, you need not travel far, just a little to the south and you can find yourself in the midst of lush nature, fine literature, and craft beer. Put yourself in a holiday frame of mind, and enjoy the intoxicating delight of books and beer!

Description: Five-star Service with Heart. The moment you walk through the doors of the Tempus Hotel, our staff will greet you with warm smiles and friendly service. With passion and sincerity, we strive to provide the best possible service to all of our guests from all corners of the globe. Our aim is to make your stay one marked by warmth, passion, gratefulness, and most importantly, joy.City and Resort: The Ultimate Relaxing Experience. Tempus comprises two buildings that each give guests a different accommodation experience: A, which combines pop styling with minimalist design, giving guests a clear, vibrant, northern European atmosphere; and B, where you can enjoy a more classical environment using high-quality stone and classy wood furniture, escaping the rat race of the city into an air of warmth and comfort. And out of consideration for vacationing families, in September 2011 Tempus opened the four-person-room-focused Da-Dun Building, offering 84 all-new rooms in a simple grey-white checkerboard motif with twin bathrooms with European baths and balconies adorned with greenery. Overall, these new offerings create a sense of total relaxation and feel like vacationing abroad.A Gourmet Combination of East and West. The Tempus offers both Chinese and Western restaurants to satisfy all kinds of appetites. Kenting Ali Seafood Restaurant’s flagship Taichung branch is located here, and the restaurant fields its own fleet of eight fishing boats to catch its own fresh fish. Master chef Li Wenzhan puts to use his 26 years of experience to create fresh dishes with a distinctively southern Taiwanese taste. La Mode Restaurant, headed up by chef Zhong Qingtian, offers European style cooking made with locally sourced ingredients, serving up international meals that are both spectacular and healthy. Between the combination of East and West, these restaurants make the Tempus a culinary landmark for central Taiwan.Balinese Relaxation in the Middle of the City. Located next to the Tempus is a large, freshly designed recreation center where guests can swim, sunbathe, or just enjoy the sunshine and breeze amongst the coconut trees. Guests at the Tempus have unlimited access to this center, and can freely take advantage of the gym, classes, and sauna for a taste of high-quality tropical relaxation in the middle of the city.

Name: Sealuv Home-stay
Description: Yilan｜Sealuv HomestayThe Delightful Taste of The Deep Blue SeaComing out the other side of the Hsuehshan Tunnel, the world seems to become brighter the further you move away from Taipei city! On your way to the Wushi Marina, you roll down the window and look out to your right at the ocean. Amid the row of ocean-view guesthouses along Waiao Beach, you see a sign which reads “Enjoy Blue Paradise” on a wave-shaped white wall. Here in Toucheng Township of Yilan County, you’re always very close to the ocean!Make a beeline for the beach with the seawater and the sunshineEntering Sealuv Homestay from the back door, to one side, you notice a professional kitchen the likes of which is rarely seen in ordinary guesthouses. Not only is there a central food counter, they have a hotel restaurant grade oven and stainless steel freezer room. The spacious dining hall is painted white and blue in Greek style, and, overlooking Waiao Beach through the front doors, is filled with the sound of the waves breaking on the sand. Removing your shoes and walking upstairs, the guest rooms all bear the names of oceanside cities. The Greek Mykonos and Aegina rooms both employ a loft design, with comfortable sofas indoors and lounge chairs on the balcony for you to recline upon. The French Marseille and Balinese Kuta rooms employ a European South seas style decor to provide visitors with a peaceful vacation time.In contrast to this, the other Sealuv edifice employs a medieval Greek style. The Sun God Apollo room on the first floor has a wading pool from which you can admire the ocean. Indoors, you can enjoy the comfort of the steam room. Similar in layout, the Moon Goddess Diana room has a home theatre system in the living room, as well as a television in the bedroom. Entering the Goddess of Beauty Venus room from the back door, you can enjoy the expansive seaview from the balcony, and delight in watching the sunrise from the comfort of your bed. Yet the most breathtaking scene must surely be on the 65-inch liquid crystal display with full surround sound audio system furnishing the God of the Sea Poseidon room. From the balcony, take the staircase upwards and discover your own private outdoor pool.Every delicious mouthful is fresh from the seaAs every gourmand who travels to Sealuv Homestay surely knows, after night falls, you are in for a flavorful feast! Your host Brother Cong introduces each local ingredient and freshly caught seafood delicacy in detail. Flying fish caviar, whitebait, and seaweed prepared cold with special dressing taste sweet and refreshing. Then comes a plate of carefully selected sashimi from the local fish market, meticulously prepared sweet shrimp, neritic squid and the rare mackerel bonito served with special sauce gives the sensation that the ocean waves are dancing on your tongue. Gently steamed bowls of chawan mushi (savoury egg custard) with fresh prawns, clams, and broccoli harmonize perfectly with the delicious flavor of katsuobushi (dried skipjack tuna flakes). The main course is perfectly broiled red blowfish with a sprinkle of salt and pepper or shichimi spicing. Each bite of fish is bursting with zesty sweetness. Served with a bowl of stewed pork over rice and homemade daikon pickle, washed down with a bowl of warm ginger fish broth, and followed by a dessert consisting of coconut cream purple rice congee and a glass of white wine.Not only do you get to enjoy an evening banquet, you can savor a European style breakfast in the morning sunshine. A delicious breakfast embraced by the sea breeze provides the perfect start to a beautiful day. Your cordial host, Brother Cong, happily suggests a travel itinerary for you: the Lanyang Museum, followed by Toucheng old street and the paragliding base. And don’t forget the privately owned local restaurants.Enjoy a beautiful place to liveWhen Brother Cong was young, he left Yilan and moved to Sanchong in New Taipei City. Yet he always maintained an indescribable affinity for the Toucheng area and, at that time, he made a promise to his young self that he would one day return. In the year that the SARS epidemic broke out, the industry that Brother Cong worked in underwent massive changes. He suddenly found himself following a course which he had not planned but which somehow seemed perfectly arranged. Sometime before, he had seized the chance when housing prices were low to buy a house in Yilan in order to give his frequently ill son more opportunities to be close to nature. It suddenly occurred to Brother Cong that it would be best to return to Yilan and try his hand at opening a guesthouse. “First the guests benefit, then the locality benefits, and only afterwards do you yourself benefit.” According to Brother Cong, Sealuv Homestay isn’t just a guesthouse, it’s a place to appreciate life. From the very beginning, he went against local custom, constructing the main entrance facing the beach while the back door faced out onto the street. He was even ridiculed by his neighbors for this decision. Yet he was determined to place prime importance on the living environment and integrate it all with a gourmet restaurant. “Many people see operating a guesthouse as a part time business, a side job. In fact this is a kind of specialized occupation, in which there is much professional knowledge.” By nature, Brother Cong is very particular about the details. It was this character which allowed him to realize the vacation space of his dreams. He hopes that when you arrive, you’ll encounter Sealuv Homestay’s unique brand of happiness.

Description: Penghu｜Summerya HouseA Place Overflowing With Sparkling Summer WatersCrossing the vast blue ocean, your boat anchors at Penghu island’s Magong Harbor. You set off along County Highway 203 for the distant city district in the north, eventually turning onto Township Road 11. Roll down the car window and let the blue sky and white clouds welcome you to the start of your journey. You arrive at Summerya House; a sunny-yellow vacation ground situated along the intertidal zone, where worries dissolve and summer cheer prevails.Inn dog and the tide: therapeutic and heartwarmingEntering the brilliant yellow building, the smile of your host Summer is as amiable as the summertime sun. Boss, the inn’s dog, circles your legs with a frisbee in his mouth, guiding you across the red-tile floor and by the solid wood table, after which you step into the sun-soaked backyard encircled by the tide. Boss runs excitedly across the lawn chasing the frisbee, you and he soaking in the ocean breeze as you chase each other around. In the sweltering afternoon, as the tide gradually rises, seawater covering the rocky seashore, Boss lazes around, too. As you sit in wooden chairs facing the ocean and listen to the burbling tide, you feel your own insignificance in the face of nature’s majesty. You also sense how fortunate you are; though you own nothing at all, at the same time, you have it all.Each room at Summerya has its own name, and each name reveals a little secret about this place. The Pure Sea Breeze room is located on the second floor and has ceilings just as lofty as the ocean winds. From the attached outdoor balcony, you have a clear view of the seaweed draped over the seaside rocks revealed by the receding tide, and the azure ocean waters at high tide. The Serene Starry Skies room also has a spacious balcony from which you might as well greet the evening stars, inviting you outside to take a stroll and enjoy the sparkling night sky. The Azure Seas room has an entire wall of floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the ocean. The beautiful ocean vista will keep you captivated all night until the first rays of the new day sun appear over the horizon. The following morning, follow your nose to the breakfast table where two slices of perfectly toasted bread with ham and eggs, a crispy salad with rich dressing, and a fragrant cup of coffee are waiting to wake up your belly. The simple yet rich flavors provide the perfect start to the day.Heartfelt regard for this piece of land, this stretch of seaRecalling the first time she saw the original piece of land where Summerya House now stands, extroverted and lively hostess Summer makes a silly face and exclaims, “It was practically in ruins!” Summer’s hometown is in the Lugu township of Nantou county. Having grown up in the mountain forests, Summer had a kind of inexpressible yearning for island life. At 17, she had saved up enough money from her part-time jobs to take a trip to Penghu, and it was that visit which left an indelible impression on her. From then on, she would seize any chance she got to go relax on Penghu island. After starting to date host Michael, Summer dragged him over to visit her beloved island. Little did she know that for Michael, Penghu would also be love at first sight! The moment he was able to wrap up the business at hand, he unhesitatingly decided to move to Penghu, the place that both he and Summer were longing for, to start a new life together and construct the beautiful Summerya House.After operating Summerya House for exactly ten years, another place that they both really liked came up for sale, the place where Oasis Hotel now sits. When asked why they wanted to create Oasis Hotel, Michael gave a mysterious answer, “Operating guesthouses is a path of no return; once you’ve begun, you end up investing all of your resources.” Perhaps it is precisely their sincere love of this land, their high self-demands, and the pull of destiny that conspired to establish them in the life that they now find themselves.Their backs to the azure ocean as they share with us their ideas about operating guesthouses, Summer and Michael laugh in unison when they get to the happy moments and listen attentively to each other when discussing the times things didn’t go as intended. Their seemingly very different personalities tacitly complement one another on account of their mutual love. In the same way, coming to Penghu from the distant main island of Taiwan, their love of the place has crystalized into the two guesthouses known as Summerya House and Oasis Hotel.Remembering the embrace of the ocean vista and the bustling journeySummerya House is like a benevolent friend who is always there to listen to your troubles and to share in your happiness. Sometimes there are layers of shape-shifting clouds, at others a vast, serene body of water. No matter if it’s early morning or late evening, no matter which season it may be, they always have a new and beautiful surprise for you. Coming to Summerya House, it’s best to bring your most sincere state of mind, and you are sure to forge a wonderful friendship!

Pure water has nurtured rich aquatic plants and the park become a habitat and feeding place for nearby birds, insects, and frogs. Professional narrators lead visitors through the programs of urban farmer experience, cycling migratory bird, equestrian riding, grass skiing, and many other enriching activities for parent and child to experience together, with a deep sense of ecological and conservation enlightenment. Four room types with different Spanish story themes, "Flamenco," "Isabella," "Antonio," and "San Diego," each room is equipped with elegant exotic handmade rosewood furniture and has balconies facing the canal and the East Rift Valley Mountains. Name_c: 熊麋鹿了幸福手作民宿
Description: Nantou｜Bear Meets MooseThe unparalleled cuteness of a Japanese zakka-style guesthouseWe’re really lost this time! Various guesthouse signs stand along either side of the road in Taomi Village, yet our fabled super-cute destination is nowhere to be found. Turning this way and that on the country lanes, we finally arrive at the Bear Meets Moose guesthouse. No wonder we got lost. They purposely have no sign!Dreamlike hosts straight out of Japanese mangaYou enter the pink building of the Bear Meets Moose guesthouse. Spacious, warm and bright, the style is rustic Japanese and there is a smell of cinnamon in the air. Light-colored wooden bookshelves hold all kinds of cute miscellaneous goods. Of course, the leading characters of this guesthouse - bear and moose - are hiding in every corner! No matter if it’s armwrestling moose and black bear, or white bears with moose antlers designed by the guesthouse owner, each wears a welcoming smile just for you!The most unexpected thing is that this cute, dreamlike, fairytale guesthouse is actually the creation of two grown boys, Jerry and Ethan. Jerry’s nickname is Tu-Tu-Ge (or Rabbit Brother), a reference to Tukisiro Yukito from the Japanese manga Cardcaptor Sakura. Both Jerry and Ethan appear as if they have just emerged from the kind of manga adored by young girls, with their fair, clear skin, eyes like crescent moons, and mouths always turned up at the corners in a smile.Afternoon tea prepared by the hosts is ready and waiting for you, but the best thing is that you get to choose your preferred mug from their rich and varied collections. Tea and handmade cookies are available around the clock here. You can even sign up for Jerry and Ethan’s own DIY dessert workshop, donning a cute apron in this cute house to make cute aromatic cookies together!A mansion fit for young ladiesBear Meets Moose is absolutely a mansion fit for young ladies; not a gold-and-jade kind of luxuriousness, but rather the kind of sweet and gorgeous environment that young girls dream of. A lavender-colored calico sofa furnishes the first floor common space, and a life-sized stuffed bear sits there awaiting your embrace. Even the wooden tree adorning the wall and ceiling spreads out overhead in layered shapes resembling a cloud, a butterfly and a heart!Each room is painted in tender colors, the favorite being the Tiffany blue room on the third floor where the ceiling is cut into diamond-shaped lines and adorned with a crystal light fixture. There is also the Rilakkuma room on the first floor where the doors are decorated with a big bear’s head and paws asking you to “give me five” before you enter. Furthermore, room and bathroom are furnished with a heater and a bed of the same quality as the Hilton hotel chain. Each and every guest is guaranteed a sweet night’s sleep.Joy fills the space inside and outYou wake up in the morning and push open the balcony doors. The sight of blue sky and green grass raises your spirits. Next, you go down stairs and find Jerry and Ethan working together to make the breakfast of your choice: a savory American-style meal, sweet banana and chocolate waffles, or toast and homemade jam. Breakfast is served with hot tea or coffee, giving the day a sumptuous and delightful start. After breakfast, walk out into the vast outdoor park area and discover even more pleasant surprises. Apart from the ecological pond and the four-seasons pathway, there is even a pool shaped like a cupid’s heart. Near the pool is a spacious barbecue area with the option to order barbecued suckling pig. Time flies in such a place, but each moment leaves a cheerful memory.

Name: Huanman Shitiping Homestay
Description: Hualian｜ Adagio ShihtipingA Slow Travel Journey Between Mountains and SeaTime seems to slow down beneath clear blue skies as you follow the Hualian-Taitung Coastal Highway (Provincial Highway 11) from Changbin township northward to Fengbin. Pulling off into the Shitiping ocean-lookout rest area, you arrive at today’s destination: Adagio Shihtiping. At a slow, relaxed pace, you set off on your exclusive journey.The enchanting elegance of mountain and seaCrossing grassy fields and ascending stone steps with the Pacific Ocean spread out right before your eyes, you push open the front doors and are greeted by the faint smell of solid wood and the smiles of your cordial hosts. Gentle piano music plays in the background as you take in the ocean vista beyond the windows and any tension you’ve brought with you slowly fades away. Laying your luggage to one side, you enter the main hall and enjoy the afternoon array of self-serve refreshments consisting of fresh seasonal fruit, handmade indigenous desserts, and fresh coffee. Sitting beside floor-to-ceiling windows and gazing at the captivating coastal vistas, your spirits feel soothed by the waves gently lapping the shore and the clouds drifting carefree through the sky.You peruse the local indigenous artwork in the main hall. With their roots in the natural world, these works of art create yet another fascinating landscape for the delight of travelers. With their insistence upon a win-win community philosophy, all Adagio Inn branches are making connections between local art and the natural environment.Enjoy pampered intimacy in any of seven private ocean-view roomsService personnel considerately help you choose the room key and the aromas best suited to your tastes, adding to the pleasure of the travel experience. Each keychain is unique, with indigenous markings that represent different romantic stories and cultural elements. Once you choose your favorite relaxing aroma from several unique herbal bath creams, the housekeeper will swap the shower products in your room for your preferred fragrance so that bath time may become a journey back to your most comfortable self.As you take off your shoes and walk up the wooden stairs, the coziness of this house reveals itself. Lounging in the spacious common room, with its assortment of magazines, two hardwood tables and roomy sofa, you can enjoy a slow-paced, cheerful mountain holiday by the seaside even without leaving the comforts of the B&B.The 330-square meter space allows each of the seven rooms to have its own special ocean view and independent open balcony. Whether you find your own comfy corner to laze around in or head out of Shitiping for a stroll, there is no need to add the stress and haste of a travel plan to your vacation. Just find your favorite spot and stay put and let the clouds and mist of the mountains drift slowly through your state of mind.Diverse breakfast dishes, slow travel with beautiful sceneryIn the brilliant morning sunlight, you stroll into the main hall to enjoy a delicious breakfast of warm congee accompanied by an array of tidy side dishes made from healthy local ingredients and served on a three-by-three square of nine small porcelain plates a la Chinese calligraphy paper and a bowl of refreshing fish soup, leaving both body and soul feeling nourished and satisfied. Before leaving, you bid farewell to the gorgeous scenery outside the floor-to-ceiling windows. Your heart suddenly softens as your body unconsciously unloads some of its usual burden. As the stress of the usual struggle for survival is cast aside, you become aware that the thing you needed to warm your heart, after all, was a date with the mountains and sea at Adagio Shihtiping.

Description: Tainan｜Sai Kau Kin Old HouseGold in the Gutter, An Old House that Spans Three CenturiesWalking at an unhurried pace through the narrow streets of the old capital city, you turn down Xinyi Street, walking past a mixture of residences both old and new. Eventually, you stop before an old wooden door painted white with couplets handwritten on red paper framing the doorway - on the horizontal scroll above the door are the characters for Sai Kau Kin Old House. You lightly push the door open, feeling the wealth of stories it must contain, and are seemingly transported a century into the past to a beautiful bygone time.The story begins with a smelly riverSai Kau Kin (literally “The Bank of the Open Sewer”) is the name of the northernmost tributary in Wu Tiao Gang (“Five Channels Harbor”). In olden days, it was used for the storage and transportation of the city’s sewage waters, hence the rather smelly sounding name. Built in 1897, the old house of today’s visit is located on the bank of this river channel. After construction of the Tainan Canal was completed, the accumulating silt and sludge filled up the channel, at which time residents in the area began to expand their dwellings outward and upward, creating the Sai Kau Kin living environment that we see today.As you set foot in Sai Kau Kin Old House, the simple wooden construction, the bamboo and wicker furniture exhibits the classical style of life in Tainan. James, the owner of the guesthouse, chose the name Sai Kau Kin Old House in the hopes of preserving the local culture, and of giving people a place to enjoy a life of freedom and ease. The roof beams overhead, the pebble-inlaid flooring underfoot, and the red brick wall all preserve the traces of history. More than a hundred years ago, during the era of Japanese occupation, the Japanese came to Tainan to implement plans for urban renewal and tore down many old city walls and buildings. The workers from the local harbors collected these bricks dating back to the era of Dutch occupation and the Ming and Qing dynasties, using them to build their own houses.Deep conversations with an old soulThis is a house that spans three centuries, as well as James’s old family home. Over forty years ago, James’s father bought this old house to provide his parents with a place to enjoy their golden years in peace. However, his parents later moved elsewhere, after which time this old house sat vacant for over twenty years. It wasn’t until 2011 that James decided to return to live in Tainan, with the belief that, “The true value of Tainan is to be found in these old laneways, these old houses, and this culture.” Thus he set about rebuilding the old building into a guesthouse with the intention of sharing memories and stories of the past with his travelling guests. Illuminated by the warm sunshine, travelers climb the steep wooden steps, arriving at the “Ballast Room” which is decorated with collected items from James’s travels through Europe when he was a young man. “This house is like a centenarian, it actually has a soul!” Continuing on, James invites you to walk barefoot upon the wooden floorboards, which sing their creaky song with every step you take.As you climb even higher, you reach the top-floor sleeping quarters. On a peaceful afternoon, you recline on the old sofa lost in thought, and looking out across the sloping open balcony which has no enclosing walls, you see all the neighboring rooftop balconies. Turning around, you notice that behind you there is another sliding door which connects to the “Matsu Room” in the attic. Looking out from the small hatch-like window, you feel like a child again, hiding in a small corner and peering out at the scenery of the laneways below. In the tranquility of night, you close your eyes, the gentle smell of rushes accompanies you as you drift into dreams of olden days.Still, the story of an old city continuesIn the morning, with Sai Kau Kin Old House as your starting point, you begin to walk along Xinyi Street. This place is different than other cities - there are no high-rise apartment buildings, only short old single-story houses one after another. These gifts that time and history have left to the city reveal the culture and enchanting atmosphere of which the people of Tainan are so proud.Xinyi Street lies between the Matsu Building and the Jifu Temple, and so receives the protection of these two great deities. It is the kind of precious land found in legends, and the place where James was born. After growing up, he backpacked around Europe and Asia, travelling to Germany, Singapore, Hong Kong, and China, even experiencing the fall of the Berlin Wall, the Tiananmen Square incident and other significant historical events, all of which nourished him to become who he is today. Afterwards, he attended advanced courses at Tokyo College of Photography. After returning to Taiwan James and his wife first decided to return to Tainan to establish their own photography studio. After striving for more than twenty years, they happened to encounter the Foundation of Historic City Conservation and Regeneration. Deeply moved by their philosophy, it was after this time that James began to operate his guesthouse and put down roots in the local culture.Beyond the operation of his guesthouse, James also devotes his efforts to putting on all kinds of different activities pertaining to arts and culture, establishing Sai Kau Kin Old House as an arts and culture space to increase interaction and exchange within the community. Check-in to Sai Kau Kin, sip a cup of tea, savour the slow passage of time, and look forward to the memories written down by each and every traveler who comes by to visit.

Description: Firefly Farm is located on the hillside at the junction of the protected forest and the upstream of Nanshi River in Fuxing Village, Tongsiao Township, surrounded by the green hills in three directions. A babbling brook flows across the valley and slowly passes through the front of the house. A courtyard covered with floral. It is a typical quiet Sanhe Yuan farmhouse. Firefly Farm offers visitors the activities including watching fireflies, listening to birds, tea and chat, swimming and playing with water. It is the best place to enjoy the countryside snacks in an arranged vacation.   Covered with wetlands around the park, the place is rich in fireflies during the annual spring season. At night, mountains and waters, in front of the house and behind the house, are dotted with charming flickering fireflies; therefore the name "Firefly Farm." Located halfway up the mountain, it is a clean environment with minimal pollution, so every year from March to November you can enjoy Luciola ficta Olivier, Pyrocoelia analis, and Luciola anceyi flying in the mountains dotting the lights. It is one of nature's most beautiful pictures.   Firefly Farm is a comprehensive B&B that integrates the concepts of nature, health and sustainability. It is located in the Firefly Ecological Restoration Area and provides a variety of services. It aims to allow every visitor to experience the process of relaxation, learning and self-healing while getting close to nature. The farm's services include accommodation, catering, DIY experiences, ecological tours, environmental education, and professional forest healing activities. Whether you are a traveler pursuing leisure or a friend who desires to relax physically and mentally, you can find your own way to relax here.

Name: Lou Zai Xia Homestay
Description: The Lou Zi Xia Traditional-Style Taiwanese Bed & Breakfast was planned and renovated by Kinmen National Park and operated by the Cai sisters from Qiong Lin Community. Three sisters manage No. 79, 92, and 105. The B&B includes 12suites accomodating up to 34 people. Groups and individuals welcome. Facilities include a BBQ grill and ingredients. After spending a day around the island, travelers can come back and barbecue, sip tea, or chat with friends under a starry night. Enjoy the serenity and a break from the stress and bustle of the city. As an environmentally-friendly B&B, Lou Zi Xia Traditional-Style Taiwanese Bed & Breakfast complies with the Kinmen Low-Carbon Program by not automatically providing disposable toiletries or changing bedding and towels for guests staying more than one night. Qiong Lin Community is located in the center of the island, and is one of its representative communities. The original name for this area, “Pinglin,” came from the forests that used to grow nearby. It has been frequented by famous people since the Ming dynasty, when one of the emperors bestowed an honorary inscribed board from which the current name, “Qiong Lin,” is derived. A number of traditional-style Taiwanese buildings, simple and elegant, with natural charm, have been preserved here. The largest of these is the ancestral temple. During times of war, tunnels were dug around the island and it had a heavy military atmosphere; now it is open to the public. Qiong Lin was home to a number of successful scholars during the Ming and Qing dynasties, and therefore a number of ornate official residences can still be viewed here. The ancestral temples are full of inscribed boards celebrating the scholars’ achievements, and in addition to the main Cai Family Temple, several more representing the branches of the family can be found in Qiong Lin. One building houses two of these temples. Each of the temples provides interesting sights, and along with Yi Gu Tang and two of Feng Shi Ye (Wind Lion Gods) have been designated second-grade historical sites.
