Name: FISH hostel - ΙΧΘΥΣ †
Description: New Taipei｜Fish HostelTake a Free-Spirited Journey to YinggeOh, you travelers who wander aimlessly to the ends of the world like a fish swimming the world’s oceans, where do you want to travel to today? Travelling wherever you will with your pack on your back, you arrive at the Yingge train station where, across the way, your eyes are drawn to a building with aquamarine blue window frames. That is the blue, the color of freedom, from which the home of a traveler is constructed - Fish Hostel.A traveler’s home, a rest station while journeying the worldAccording to legend, a gigantic parrot roaming the blue skies once decided to settle on a mountain ridge in the western part of New Taipei City. The moment it perched itself, the story of “Parrot Brother Rock” (literal translation of  Ying Ge Shi) was born and slowly passed on by word of mouth to one day become the “Oriole Song” (literal translation of  Ying Ge) we know today. Over the years, the traveler’s melody was added to the Oriole Song. Fish Hostel sits directly across from the Yingge Train Station, perfectly situated to welcome those drifting souls to take a rest along their journey.As you enter the main hall, a large tree limb is used as a merchandise display to the left side of the entrance. A variety of small products from far-off locations hangs from the branches. Available for purchase are ethnic clothing items with tribal designs, handmade jewelry, and much more. Your host Emma also loves travel, and has brought back a rich and diverse world with which to decorate Fish Hostel. “Since this is a traveler’s home, I wanted to give everyone a peaceful and comfortable feeling!” One entire wall on the first floor is covered in graffiti principally composed of blue and white colors, creating an ambiance of peace and harmony. The design was entirely created by Emma who gave life to her ideal through each brush stroke. Emma’s conviction is that, through her skillful creation, fish that once wandered to the ends of the world without a home now have a place to return to. She hopes to energize the travelers that come her way.A little backpacker’s abode built from bountiful graffitiKicking off your shoes, you head upstairs where you find tidy rows of simple wooden bunk beds that have supported the travel dreams of travelers from around the world. Besides backpacker accommodations, Fish Hostel also offers two- and four-person rooms. The keyring for the room shows a fish swimming through a little heart, like a nimble fish which can, in the blink of an eye, bring you back to the Little Sun Room. The Little Sun Room has its own private balcony and ample comforting daylight. The light bathes the warm tones of the room in which the compelling breeze lightly sways your beautiful dreams. A hand-painted wall with ocean-blue as its base color leads you along to the Big Sun Room. The color designs lead you to the splendid yellow flowers blooming in the Big Sun Room, as if keeping watch over anyone who sleeps soundly in the two double beds. A soft, bright green floor mat covers the floor beneath the beds, to allow guests the utmost level of relaxation and enjoyment.ΙΧΘΥΣ is the Greek word for fish, as well as an important spiritual symbol for Fish Hostel. In the early days of Christianity, when believers were under persecution from the Roman Empire, they would use the Greek word for fish with graceful arcs drawn above and below as a secret sign to identify each other’s status as believers. “It is my hope that every traveler who comes to Fish Hostel can find companions that they are compatible with, as well as to be in the peaceful presence of Jesus.” Emma says that fish are just like our souls; we are all in the middle of a journey, step-by-step to complete our own lives.A traveler’s chance encounter leads to the completion of lifeSurprisingly, the multi-talented host of Fish Hostel, Emma, redid her university test in order to choose her beloved industrial arts design program. During her student years, she worked as a pottery teacher, using her income to accumulate an impressive store of travel memories from all over. Just like the rich and diverse decor of the living room, Emma used movement to fulfill her heart and spirit. During the summer break of her second year of university, she was an artist in residence in Jiufen. She met many friends thanks to that opportunity. “They were all doing what they wanted to do, and it showed me that life can be very simple.” After two months in residence, Emma had imagined her ideal blueprint for her life, and the dream of opening a guesthouse slowly started to sprout in her mind. She recalls, “I didn’t want to wait until some time in the distant future. I could do what I wanted to do even while I was a student.” After she had made up her mind, she rode all over on her scooter to find a location. She found it on day three. By day seven she had created her business plan! Her past travel experience along with her meticulous craftsmanship all helped to nurture the development of Fish Hostel! “Our lives are always full of speed and light, and Fish Hostel opens a little chink in that speed.” The walls are covered in passionate messages, as well as Emma’s own hand-drawn map of local travel spots, awaiting travelers to continue to add to the map. At Fish Hostel, travel is like an ongoing dialogue. At Fish Hostel, no matter what language is used, whether vocal or silent, whether the dialogue is outwards or inwards; souls that are in love with travel will continue to rush forth as if pushed by a warm current, hurrying onwards for the next ocean journey.

Name: Longmen House B&B
Description: Longmen House Bed & Breakfast was built for the Chen family in 1924 in the traditional Hokkien sanheyuan style, which incorporates three structures around a courtyard, and has been converted into a bed & breakfast in the hopes of sharing the beauty of Penghu’s traditional fishing-village style. When you first turn the oxcart-wheel door and enter Longmen House Bed & Breakfast, you’ll be met with a carefully crafted tiled map of Penghu. Then, after knocking on the stained wooden door, you’ll set foot on a red-tile floor and enter the central courtyard, flanked by traditional tiled windows and equipped with bamboo chairs and redwood bed, like a trip backward in time. The outdoor pavilion was hand-built by Mr. Chen from driftwood over the course of four months, and sits near another recently completed “Penghu boat” pavilion which is perfect for lying down in and enjoy the starry nights. One of life’s great pleasures is dining in these cool pavilions, enjoying a fresh Penghu seafood barbeque under the beautiful nighttime skies. Or you could sit in one of the second-floor balconies, looking out across the starry night sky and enjoying the sea breeze as you sip on a cup of coffee or tea. During these tranquil nights, troubles and stress just seem to melt away. Come visit us at Longmen House! Website: http://www.longmenhouse.com.tw

Name: Jingxin Yuan Xiang Ju Homestay
Description: Sun Moon Lake’s Jing Xin Yuan Rural Bed and Breakfast is located in Seshui Community near Sun Moon Lake (Yuchih (Yuchi) Township, Nantou County). On Provincial Highway 21, on Zhongtan Road after passing Dayan Tunnel, take a right and enter. Conveniently located, with nearby tourist sites including Sun Moon Lake, Formosa Aboriginal Culture Village, Taiwan Adventist College, Lienhuachih, Shueili (Shuili) Checheng, and Puli, this is the ideal place to stay on weekends or vacations when planning your trip to Nantou. Seshui Community resembles a lotus blossom in a valley, featuring a beautiful environment, great scenery, and rich produce and ecological resources. Community resides worked together to build a very special ecological village which was selected as one of the Top 10 Classic Villages in 2007. It produces two specialty products, the first of which is Seshui Pottery, made from top-quality Baixian clay, which does not require the use of glaze. The oxidized ashes given off by the wood-fired baking process gives the finished pottery a varied appearance, making each piece a special, unique product. The other speicalty product is Seshui Royal Tea, which derives its name from being one of Taiwan’s top quality black teas. It was once the tea of choice for Japanese emperors; the name also refers to serving tea. All tea leaves are organic, handpicked with one bud and two leaves, and free of fertilizers or pesticides. Excellent quality guaranteed their place in the Assam cultural revival. We welcome you to try out this special “Japanese imperial tea.”

Name: Goodian coffee , Bed & Breakfast
Description: Taoyuan｜Goo Dian Coffee HouseA happy little house beside a verdant green valleyYou drive out of the city on a winding country road and head deep into the mountains. Opening the car window, the breeze brushes by smelling of green grass. Slowing down the car, the layers of greenery outside the window put you in a fine mood. Turning a corner, you come upon a traveler’s relay station in the mountains - Goo Dian Coffee House is subtly located in a valley on Lala Mountain, embraced by the blue sky and green environment and just waiting to bring you in touch with the natural world.Situated in relaxed and carefree mountainsShutting off the engine, you hear the wind flowing through the mountains. As you breathe the cool mountain air, you smile and raise your head to take in your surroundings; a simple wooden house sits in the embrace of the green mountain forests. House and forest merge together, creating a harmonious scene. Tiantian (literally means “sweet”), the enthusiastic little Corgi, rushes forward to welcome you with his big, round eyes. You follow Tiantian into the relaxing environment of Lala Mountain.Attached to the wooden reception building is a two-level outdoor coffee terrace. You sit comfortably in a chair sipping a cup of flavorful coffee. The terrace is without windows and doors, so there is no separation between you and the grandeur and magnificence of the mountain range. The Daman creek flows by, revealing the vitality of nature. After a heavy rain, you may have the good fortune to see white gauze-like clouds enshrouding the emerald green mountains. Those clouds also envelope your worries, and you feel convinced that all your troubles will slowly scatter with the clouds and mist.Serene life in the mountain valleyIn your bedroom, host Lin has created a cozy, simple decor that mirrors the rustic character of the mountains. In the three double rooms - the Maple Leaf, Ginkgo, and Wistaria rooms - elegant color schemes further accentuate the endless green scenery outside the windows. Lying lazily upon the soft bed, you can admire the myriad transformations of the mountains as you drift naturally into slumberland. The three-room Sakura Suite is large enough to accommodate a large family on vacation together. In the afternoon, playful children can feed the koi fish in the nearby pond while adults chat about life in the living room. The wooden swing hanging outside the house brings innocent smiles to the faces of young and old alike. In the evening, you prepare a simple late-night snack. After everyone has eaten and drunk to their heart’s content, you sit enjoying each other’s company. It is such simple things that fill life with happiness.A generous and friendly ambiance is the best spiceLin lives here with his younger brother and parents, working together to operate Goo Dian Coffee House and maintain the vast forest park surrounding it. His cute, taciturn father has created an area for raising special and unusual animals, while his mother is responsible for cooking and taking care of the fruit trees. For the convenience of travelers from afar, Goo Dian provides both breakfast and dinner using vegetables from the local mountain landscape to satisfy the taste bud of their guests. Fresh, crisp bamboo shoots, crispy yet tender trout that is grilled to perfection - with fine skill, the chef produces dish after dish of beautiful, seasonal cuisine, with a mother’s home-cooked touch. It is almost as if you’ve returned to your own home away from home in the mountains.Early spring is the time to appreciate the sakura blossoms and in summer, you can savor the fragrant sweetness of juicy peaches. Winter is the time to marvel at a romantic landscape of snow-covered mountains. Stay for a single night at Goo Dian Coffee House and allow your body and spirit to be completely absorbed into the embrace of Lala Mountain. Leave the gloom of the city far behind and return to nature to enjoy the beauty of mountain life.

Name: Season Star
Description: My wife and I met in college and our family has been growing tea in Alishan for several generations. As the eldest son, I returned with my wife to my hometown after getting married, originally planning to make a living growing tea. However, after hearing about new trends in the leisure industry, I started considering changing the family business. My wife and I spent 6 years studying Chinese and Western cooking, baking, making drinks, bed and breakfast operation, restaurant management, and obtaining a license. My wife, who had never studied design before, managed to create a plan using paintbrush, and in 2006, our dream finally became a reality. Featuring a southern European style, the building’s design includes light yellow walls, red roof tiles, and wood strip patterns, displaying a rich European recreational style, with distinctly separate front and rear buildings. On a bright, clear day, it looks particularly lovely and inviting. Pension Seasonstar is located at Alishan Xiding, with views of the sunrise, sunset, and magnificent sea of clouds. As this is the famous Alishan tea area, surrounded by mountain mists in the distance all year round, the tea grown here is particularly sweet, smooth, and refreshing. We like to make friends with travelers by sharing our lives and feelings with them. An elderly Japanese man and his sister came to visit the Japanese colonial era elementary school, lovers have proposed to each other here, and wedding photographs have been taken here. Sometimes a entire family comes out to enjoy this place, and really, the happiest moment is being able to make our friends smile.

Name: David SamStrong Villa
Description: Taitung｜David SamStrong VillaA seaside mountain vacation with sunlight and shadeDriving down the eastern coast, your car turns a corner and leaves the ocean behind. Another left turn and you head towards the entrance to Hsiaoma Hoping Mountain as an alley opens up between flowers to one side of the road. Wind ripples the trees and grass beside the alley as you make your way expectantly towards the end of the road where David SamStrong Villa is situated. You can’t help but wonder what kind of pleasant surprises await.A tender dream stacked in layers upon the hillsideA gray building sits upon the hillside. The concrete walls of David SamStrong Villa maintain their original color and are coated with a monolithic finish, the building itself square-shaped, like a stack of toy building blocks. Suddenly, a burst of bright yellow enters your line of sight. As David, the host of this guesthouse, explains, that splash of color represents his frame of mind. Every day is a splendid vacation under such blue skies.Originally employed as an engineer in a computer company, David has a resonant laugh and a soft heart. While performing his military service here in Taitung, David fell in love with the beautiful mountains and ocean vistas of the area. In order to give his elderly parents a place to retire and rest, he built a personal residence in the Taitung hills. At that time, now 10 years past, he spent his days tending the fruits, vegetables, and plants in his gardens. Three years ago, he began planning construction of a bed and breakfast, in the hopes of introducing even more people to the beauty of the simple life. Once built, he named this second building by combining his English (David) and Chinese (SamStrong) names. Thus, the jocular name David SamStrong Villa came into being.Framing the various postures of sunlightDavid limits admission to a single group of travelers at one time. In his villa, you can relax and live it up, and are guaranteed your favorite corner to lounge in. First floor accommodations consist of two double rooms which exhibit simple concrete-gray walls sprinkled with large splashes of yellow decor, yet are devoid of fancy furniture. Instead, large windowpanes allow the vastness of the Pacific Ocean to spill indoors. The semi-open design allows you to linger in the courtyard, strolling along the verdant garden paths. Alternately, you can sit in your doorway in a comfortable loveseat, savoring the sun-bathed hills in the distance. You can also stroll out behind the stairs, finding a wall fashioned with rectangular openings of different sizes through which the sunlight dances and plays in magical ways all day long.Climbing the stairs to the second floor, you find a living room and a kitchen in the same simple, down-to-earth style. Gray walls accentuate the natural warmth of the wooden furniture. David’s own handmade dried fruit preserves sit to one side of the dining table for the enjoyment of his guests. Two lounge chairs, ideal for sunbathing and admiring the emerald green mountainside, await you on the balcony outside. Gazing towards the base of the mountain, sky and sea meet at the horizon in a poetic landscape where time seems to stand still.Straightforward design highlighting spectacular viewsThe following morning, you are greeted by a table full of David’s handmade delicacies. Such things as eggs, salads, hibiscus tea, peanut butter and bread - all breakfast ingredients are organically grown and prepared by David and his mother. This distinctive, nourishing breakfast is made even more enjoyable by the blue backdrop of the Pacific Ocean beyond the windows.Light and shadow play through every corner of the semi-open and dynamic design of David SamStrong Villa. Wherever you go, you follow the tracks of sunshine and shade, whether standing or sitting or lying down. The green of the mountains and the blue of the ocean always seem easily within reach. How could a single day living in such luxury possibly be enough?

Description: Hualien｜Bears in the Forest GuesthouseBears! A Comfortable Vacation on the LakesideYour car drives into Shoufeng township, situated in Hualien county between the central and coastal mountain ranges. Hidden away down laneways and between farmers’ fields you discover Yun Shan Shui Park. Across a bridge, several small white cottages rest between white clouds, green hills, and crystal-clear waters. Bears in the Forest Guesthouse invites you to enter a verdant landscape on the side of a lake, to enjoy a comfortable vacation… with bears and the forest!Bears will enjoy your vacation with youThe wind blows across a vast field of grass spread out like a green carpet. A big bear doll stands in the doorway outfitted like a British guard to welcome you. Pushing open the wooden doors, bear dolls one after another are to be found throughout the lobby. Coming here is all about relaxing with the bears!Happy music begins to play while the large glass windows reflect the lake and the emerald green scenery beyond. You only need to slow your pace, and breathe deep the fresh clean air. Look up from the grassy lawn at the starry night sky with the natural symphony of bird and insect song surrounding you.A dreamland by the lakesideAllen, the host of Bears in the Forest Guesthouse, recalls of when he came to Hualien to serve in the military. He was attracted to the great mountains and waters, and to the good air. At that time, he established his goal to return to this place and build a comfortable little house. He planned the gardens in European style and designed the rooms with Japanese elements. Allen has help from friends with business and marketing experience. He also has ties with the locals, and his diligent efforts bring people the same satisfaction and contentment as entering the forest.The Guesthouse is made up of 12 independent little houses in five different styles, such as four-person rooms suitable for bringing your parents or your children to enjoy together. Couples or pairs, on the other hand, might choose to check into a loft or an exquisite little double room. There is a little black teddy bear friend in every room, or several cute, loveable bear dolls lying on the sofa. Every washroom has a heating system and the pleasant smell of Chinese juniper. Enjoying your own private courtyard in the dim evening light, you feel inspired to soak in the outdoor hot spring and wash away your exhaustion. Local Hualien vegetables in your mealsThe moment you check in, cute bear cookies are laid on the table before you, paired with panna cotta, Hualien sweet potato cakes, and a variety of other local snacks. You can also book in advance for a chef’s tasting menu to enjoy delicious dishes made with local ingredients. In the morning, you cross the spacious lawn on your way to the lobby to enjoy a sumptuous Taiwanese style breakfast consisting of cold-dressed lotus root, salted egg with wild bitter gourd, beef and potato stew, and sauteed salmon accompanied by a bowl of sweet potato congee for a beautiful start to the day. You set out into the breeze on a reserved bicycle to admire the deep green scenery and tranquil atmosphere of the lake. At Bears in the Forest Guesthouse, you’ll feel the warmth of the bear’s embrace.

Name: Yu Shuen Garden Homestay
Description: In front of Yu Xuan Yuan Bed & Breakfast is a green tunnel, and behind it, a pond and garden. Situated on Tainan Road 90, it is in close proximity to the hundred-year-old mango tree green tunnel, as well as fields of lotuses and paddies of rice. Looking out across the Jianan Plain, a huge expanse of greenery and fields as far as the eye can see, is an amazing experience. In the early morning or at dusk, why not take a walk or ride, watch the sun rise/set, breathe deep of the fresh air, and relax? Or how about just taking in the majestic sight of Mt. Guanzihling (Guanziling) A mere 15-minute walk will get you to the Lotus Information Center, and one kilometer to the west sits the Linchupi Cotton Trail. About five kilometers to the west lies Xiaonanhai Natural Ecological Park, and 1.5 kilometers to the north is Lianhua (Lotus) Park. Baihe Township is 4.5km south of Yu Xuan Yuan, and about 14km to the east is Guanzihling (Guanziling), a wonderful place for a drive or a ride, with the promise of hot springs at the end! Behind Yu Xuan Yuan itself sits a “secret garden” complete with fountain, lotuses, and carp, as well as a beautiful pagoda that combines classic and modern design. With fruit trees and shrubs abounding, the air is crisp and clean, making it a refreshing place to relax and listen to nature, far from the madding crowds. The lotuses are at the best between June and August each year, filling the air with fragrance — and if you want to fully enjoy them at their peak, the best time would be between 6am and 8am. In March, the cotton trees bloom, while May sees the golden shower trees on show; April and May are also when the mangoes and passionfruit are at their best, while June offers the chance to try your hand at picking fully ripened mangoes. December, meanwhile, is the perfect time to try picking, or just appreciating, the lotus roots and having a go at making lotus flour — and of course, you’ll need somewhere to spend the night too! A stay here is truly great for the mind, body, and soul. Yu Xuan Yuan Bed & Breakfast has been running for over 13 years now, and was even recognized by the Tourism Bureau, Republic of China (Taiwan) in 2011 as one of the “100 Happy Stays” and received a “Taiwan Host” award in 2012! It truly is a place well worth a visit!

Name: Qingtaoyuan B&B
Description: The owner of this B&B is Mr. CHANG, Shih-Yuan. To commemorate the ancestor, the B&B is named Qing Taoyuan Homestay representing the name of CHANG, Qing-Lai, his father; CHANG WANG Chung-Tao, the mother; and part of his own name Yuan respectively. The name is adopted in the hope that their off-springs will remember the hardship of developing the home at the very beginning and that the B&B will serve as a  Shangri-La, allowing every visitor an experience different from city life. It is an individual blue and yellow villa, resembling a castle standing tall and firm in a wide meadow. The outdoor courtyard is specifically designed and arranged by the innovative ideas of the owner decorated with stone, pavilion and recreational facilities in presenting delicate and secluded landscape guiding visitors to the dream-like fairy tale land while serving as a playground for children. The guestrooms are designed in modernized concise style adorned with wooden flooring and comfortable bedding. In this way, every room is subtly designed by the owner like his own room to provide a clean and comfortable living quality for every guest. "Kenting - Qing Taoyuan Homestay" has a great view and allows you to look far into the mountains . You may look toward the mountain ranges along the “Niu Shan Ling Mountain and further to the lake scenery of the “Lung Luan Lake” and the birds flying around there. While taking in  the dawn, be sure to take a big breath of the fresh air. When strolling in the garden, stop occasionally to find the species of the birds that are singing. Enjoy the fund of the wild field and the beauty of sunset dusk. Before turning in, do not forget to look upward and say good night to the stars. Travel is to discover another level of life! A quest for the fun of life.

We’re located away from the street and noisy traffic, instead featuring great scenic views and on clear nights a sky full of stars, or even shooting stars! It will be an unforgettable night; leave the city behind and experience this kind of life! Every person reserves a place for dreams in their heart, and should you wish to discover new surprises, take a music and flower tour and visit Arce Wisteria Bed and Breakfast.

Name: Ji Ye Jing Zhan Homestay
Description: This is a very special B&B. Its open-structured and permeable decoration is full of art spirit, showing the style of fashion and indicating the freedom and lifestyle. Surprisingly, the B&B host, Mr. Dai, is a young and cheerful man, and his friends call him Dai. He is fond of independent travel, and occasionally saw loft-style B&B's when traveling abroad. The open-structured space with no partitions and freestyle design had attracted his attention. He started to have a dream. It is hard to imagine that this humorous and friendly young man was a perfect salesman with outstanding performance in the banking industry. However, his life was filled with work. He worked long hours and attending social functions, and often came back home at late night. He suddenly realized that what he was missing when he saw his children sound asleep. At last, when he was 40, he made an important decision - to retire. He found his own way after tendering his resignation letter. He desired to make his dream come true. What he saw abroad affected him and made him eager for action, and he started to make plans. He wanted to bond with his children when it was not too late, let them grow up in a great environment, and realize his dream - running a special B&B. After thinking carefully, he settled down in Hualien - the most beautiful area in Taiwan. He spent two years completing his own buildings- from design and plan to selecting materials and constructing, and he gradually completed the perfect B&B in his mind. He owns two buildings for the B&B. Building A, with dark red brick walls, vintage electric fans, visible  pipelines and log doors, makes you go back to the 1950s. Building B, with black iron partition cabinet, leather sofa and glossy floor, shows an ornate style to make you feel like displaced in time and place. There is no other B&B like Ji Ye Jing Zhan Villa Homestay in Taiwan. Dai hopes that travelers can experience the happiness he had experienced before as long as they visit Hualien- no flight ticket, not going abroad, and no tiring flight.

It is the children call comes. But for understanding frogs and committed to it, that is her most vivid impression and joy of life .Both she and her daughter made a certificate for the narrator. She understands fully the voice of frogs, features, and characteristics. When talking about the fogs, she can speak on a subject with great familiarity, and a grin. Following their lead to observe frogs will be the most unforgettable memories of the stay. Grandma Frog Farm House, every lovely bits and pieces are all touching little stories. Name: Spring-Feng Cinnamomum Bed&Bre
Description: Spring Feng Bed and Breakfast is located in Jhongliao (Zhongliao) Township (Nantou County), facing Jiji Mountain in the east and Jiji Township in the south, and located a 35 minute drive from Sun Moon Lake. In order to experience the simple life, the owner decided to build a farm and pond on his own land after retiring. Here, he has arranged every plant and tree and included a vegetable garden. For environmental reasons, he weeds by hand, makes his own organic fertilizer, and reuses wastewater and rainwater so as not to waste natural resources. This makes the garden rich in ecology, with tree frogs, Muller’s barbets, Chinese bamboo partridges, and scops owls. During the spring, summer, and fall, the frogs begin singing in the evenings, causing quite the commotion and staring at us, wondering why people never give them a round of applause. The pleasing sound of chirping birds in the morning seems to be calling us to wake up, get out of bed, and enjoy the fresh air outside! Looking off at the mountains in the distance and watching birds flying in pairs, one cannot help but feel their heart open up and mind be at peace. The total area is approximately 9000 square meters, including 700 Taiwanese indigenous cinnamon trees. The bed and breakfast itself occupies about 2500 square meters, including a parking lot, cinnamon oil refining DIY activity, special cinnamon spiced cuisine (cinnamon chicken, golden eggs, fried rice, and tea), cinnamon products (cinnamon shampoo, body wash, mosquito repellent, hand lotion, and lip gloss). Guests can enjoy cinnamon baths with fragrant oils, helping them relax and relieve pressure.

Name: Jijivellage villa B & B
Description: Natou｜Jiji Village B&BA traditional courtyard farmhouse where time temporarily stands stillAs you pass over the Jilu Bridge, cross farmers’ fields, and survey the rolling hills, the distracting thoughts in your mind all dissipate. In a moment, you seem to transcend space and time, returning to olden days where you encounter a traditional courtyard farmhouse, majestic in its old age and exuding the genuine ambiance of 1950s Taiwan. You feel as though you’ve walked into the type of picturesque pastoral landscape described in ancient Chinese poetry. Jiji Village B&B possesses a sunny verdancy, the courtyard of a mountain getaway, and host Mr. Liu’s love of the land.Deeply felt memories of childhoodYou and your friends disembark and put both feet on the soft, grassy ground as sunlight shines through lattice covered with loofah gourd vines. You pass through the wooden front doors surrounded by spring couplets, and admire the red brick walls which bear the traces of passing time. “Come right in and have a seat!” You hear Mr. Liu’s friendly welcome as a small, yellow dog named Cachito greets you. The name Cachito originates from a Spanish folktale, and Mr. Liu regards Cachito as a gift from heaven.This spacious, modern three-building courtyard is full of layers. The sunlight and air from the front vestibule and rear courtyard are able to penetrate inside through large, wooden-framed windows, imprinting the window screens with numerous beautiful silhouettes. The huge space is divided by wooden panels and doors, and to both sides, the refreshing greenery of potted plants is seen along the hinoki promenades of the left and right buildings. The entire space encourages you to slow your pace and wander leisurely around, taking in the scenery.A true reflection of the 1950sFrom the roof beams inside to the steps in the courtyard, from the low stone walls to the courtyard well, entering this house of wood and stone is like stepping into the childhood memories of Mr. and Mrs. Liu. According to Mr. Liu, “Wood and stone are two key elements here at Jiji Village B&B, because the veins in the stone and the grain of the wood are respectively identical inside and outside. So, too, should be the mind of man and woman.” Mr. Liu hopes that all travelers who visit here can perceive the sincerity which this building emits. Pushing open the rosewood screen doors and heading to the second-floor rooms, the floorboards creaking underfoot are reminiscent of childhood days chasing siblings up and down the halls and stairs. Jiji Village offers three guest rooms in old fashioned styles. The walls of the Taiwan Fir Tree Country-Style Room are constructed from Chinese fir, and the woody aroma permeates the room. The Japanese Tatami Room is exceedingly comfortable. Yet the most romantic of all is the Classic Chinese Canopy Bed Room. Mr. Liu searched far and wide to find this traditional bed. The room is also furnished with an ornately carved dresser, embroidered red pillows, and an antique gramophone phonograph player, creating a romantic dreamland for you and your lover.A traditional farmhouse infused with modernityBeneath a single yellow light bulb, Mr. and Mrs. Liu prepare dinner beside the traditional wood burning kitchen hearth. Mr. Liu cheerfully carries out plate after plate of authentic vegetable and meat dishes; juicy bamboo shoot with meat, organic loofah gourd fresh from the garden, braised bean and pork, and healthy burdock consommé, all made with love. After the meal, you chat over the tea table off to one side of the dining room, admiring the traditional Taiwanese tea spread and delicate ceramic teaware. Mr. Liu also has a traditional Japanese tea spread with tatami seating. Hollows in the floor allow you to extend your legs comfortably as the moon shines through the windows and reflects off the tea in your cup. You walk out into the courtyard to appreciate the tranquil evening and the cool, countryside air. The summer sun, just like a farmer, rises early, illuminating the bright green lawn in the courtyard. Waking to the shadows dancing in the passion fruit orchard outside your window, you walk spritely downstairs to find that Mrs. Liu has prepared a sumptuous breakfast of refreshing salad and rice milk, reminding you of the happiness to be found in simple things.After retiring from the air force, Mr. Liu felt homesick and so decided to return to his childhood home in Nantou and start a guesthouse business. He could not have anticipated that he would encounter the devastating Jiji earthquake which rocked Taiwan on the 21st of September, 1999. That traumatic event did not dishearten Mr. Liu, instead inspiring him to begin the activity of “Orally Recounting History” where he did relief work to aid those affected by the disaster. He and Mrs. Liu set up a vendor’s stall selling Job’s tear milk on the street, using their love of their homeland to get back on their feet. First, they opened a restaurant based on all of the old, traditional recipes they could find by interviewing the local elders, inviting travelers to taste the local flavors of Jiji. Yet they never forgot their original intention to open a guesthouse. Thus, after opening their restaurant and winery, they devoted themselves wholeheartedly to the operation of their guesthouse, a road that they have walked together, supporting one another all the way, using past frustrations to nurture their aspirations. They based their blueprints upon childhood memories, inviting travelers into their traditional courtyard farmhouse, to enjoy tranquility, happiness, and contentment.

Name: Golden Gate Royal Villa
Description: Looking at the map of Kinmen, Kinmen looks like a bone, and the B&B is located just above the middle of the bone in the "Hengcuo" Village. This is the fastest way for people who don't know Kinmen to find this B&B, and it is also the most impressive. Hengshan Laoye Villa is located in the natural village of Hengcuo, just in the middle of Qionglin and Housha. It is particularly located in a moderate location and has convenient transportation. It is about seven kilometers away from the city centers of Jincheng, Shanwai and Shamei, about four kilometers from Shangyi Airport, and about 12 kilometers from Shuitou Pier. It takes more than ten minutes to walk to the adjacent Qionglin Underground Tunnel Scenic Area. "Qionglin Settlement" is one of the representatives of Kinmen's traditional settlements. It retains a large number of traditional Minnan buildings with swallow-tailed horses on back. In addition, the ancestral temples are the largest and most distinctive. In addition to the "Cai Family Temple" of the main ancestral family, each house also has its own ancestral hall. Two of them are in the same three-story building, so they are known as the "Seven Eight Ancestral Halls". Someone once used Tao Yuanming's "Peach Blossom Spring" to describe the village of "Hengcuo". Therefore, the village is located in a basin surrounded by trees. So when you enter from the path, you will be very confused. But after walking a few dozen steps, you will see a stream and a large lawn. There are small fish playing in the stream and turtles bathing in the sun. The teal ducks and water birds are swimming leisurely in the river and looking for food.  You can also watch birds walking or foraging on the lawn, as if they are not afraid of people approaching. Then you will see several houses located in this basin, and the Hengshan Laoye Villa is one of them.  Especially due to its superior geographical location, natural environment and lack of excessive man-made development, it upholds the concept of symbiosis between man and the environment, creating this village like a paradise. Therefore, you can see many birds coming to live in this building, and you can also see otters, Kinmen's protected animals, here. The creek in front of the B&B is connected to the sea. You can walk 400 meters along the village path. The first thing you see is a small intertidal zone. In the intertidal zone, you can see cute mudskippers bouncing in the water. Fiddler crabs are constantly shuttling in the caves. Groups of small crabs will dig in the sand in a spiral shape when people get close. Of course, there are many unknown creatures living in this intertidal zone. Walk dozens of steps along this intertidal zone to see the beautiful, deep and boundless sea. Name: The  Lalu  Sun  Moon  Lake
Description: If there is a name that can stir your emotions, it is The Lalu(Han Bi Lo in Chinese), even if each word in the name costs a hundred million dollars. In 1901, Mr. Ito built a small wooden cabin on the Lalu Peninsula for vacation use and called it “TheFor hundreds of years, with strict entrance control, only senior governmental official, generals, prime ministers, and emperors are allowed into The Lalu. Therefore, a myth is created to this building. However, how did The Lalu  come about?In 1923, the Japanese Crown Prince Hirohito visited Taiwan and appointed The Lalu to be his official residence. He rebuilt the small wooden cabin into a two-story building and added eight guest rooms, including the east and the west wings, dining room, conference room and more. From this time on, The Lalu turned itself from a luxury vacation home into an official government guest house.In 1949, when the Chinese Nationalist Government retreated to Taiwan, The Lalu became President Chiang Kai-Shek’s hostel, used primarily for vacation use and to entertain foreign head of states.In 1998, Mr. Cheng-Yi Lai, chairman of the Shining Group, received a phone call that filled his heart with tremendous excitement and doubt. For the past 30 years, his dream was to build a world class hotel along the shores of Sun Moon Lake. The man that made the phone call indicated to him that The Lalu was for sale.However, buying this historical building was not going to be a simple task. The seller was asking for a sum of NT$ 270 million  and made it clear that it was not negotiable. It took over a year of hard work and negotiation, with the end result closing at the firm asking price of NT$ 270 million. Mr. Lai recalled and said, “Which name is always on people’s mind without ever needing any advertisement? This name has its place and historical value in public’s mind so the name itself is priceless. Even with millions that we spent on it, I think it’s still a bargain.”After 5 years and an investment of NT$ 1.86 billion, using the theory of utmost simplification of Zen style as the architectural design core from our award winning international design team, the renovation of this historical hotel began. It was rebuilt from the original palace style 6 story building, saving only its beams, columns and floor and replacing everything else. The new design divides the building into three separate building (building A, B and C) for different purposes. Building A is the main guest house. Building B is the structure that houses entertainment facilities such as the Spa, gym, Jacuzzi and Members Clubhouse. Building C includes the Villa area, conference facility, Library and parking lot. On March 3, 2002, The Lalu reopened to the public with its new design and resort style .

Name: ChooArt Villa
Description: Miaoli｜ChooArt VillaBreathe with Nature and Return to the Tranquility Embraced by the ForestThe ripples of the green pool water reflect the beautiful shadows of trees in your mind. Close your eyes and let the mountain breeze brush against your body. Passing by the Longteng Broken Bridge, you are driving on the mountain road to Sanyi, Miaoli County. When the car enters ChooArt Villa, the fragrance of flowers and plants floats in the air and a large striped-dove flies in the sky. Behind the hidden wooden door, your exclusive holiday is expecting your arrival. Here, you breathe with nature, while the mountain and woods embrace you with their beauty.Share with Nature the Leisurely Vacation in Mountain Woods Under the rooftop garden of irises, the vine-covered buildings of ChooArt Villa in the valley are beautifully arranged in a haphazard way like stylish tree houses, while staying close to nature. You enter the lobby with the floor-to-ceiling windows and doors, have a cup of coffee and rest for a bit. Sit in the sofa chair by the glass window, browse through some magazines or books, take in the scenery and just enjoy the leisurely time.Step down the outdoor stairs, and you find yourself at the pool, where the verdant camphor woods above provide you with shade. When the wind blows, the tree branches and leaves flutter, and the shadows on the spring water sway to a natural rhythm. You sit on the deck chair as your lover floats relaxingly in the water. Your cheerful mood is accompanied by the chirping of the birds. Everything is just so delightful and at ease.Sun, Tree, River, and Moon; Planting Four Relaxing Sleep SpacesBeing built along the contour of the hill, four double rooms of ChooArt share a simple character, and they breathe and live with the woods. Walking into the “Tree Spring” double room, time seems to slow down here. In the bedroom space, three camphor trees stretching up toward the light are surrounded by the glass windows. Get closer to the window, and you’d enjoy the relaxing melody composed by the bamboo forest and the creek outside. Take off your clothes and get through the U-shaped corridor by the greenery balcony, you’ll arrive at the spacious bathroom with the forest view. The “Sunny River” room offers the view of the ruins of the Broken Bridge. You may listen to the sound of running water and enjoy the quiet peace here. The sunlight penetrates the transparent floor-to-ceiling gauze curtains of the “First Sun” room, while the bed with the gauze canopy brings you a sense of the romantic holiday. You can also walk through the glass passage with the reflection of the blue sky to the bathroom. In the “Tipsy Moon” room, you can admire the enchanting starry sky and the lush scenery.Taste the Authentic Taiwanese Flavor in the Creative CuisineAs your stay at ChooArt includes two meals, you can enjoy the culinary delights that incorporate  creative ideas with local ingredients. In the evening, you step into the dining room on the second floor, where the chef will demonstrate how the food is carefully prepared in the open kitchen. There are refreshing appetizers, hearty salads, and creative dishes with a variety of artistic senses. Of course, the highlight would be the surf and turf meal combined with the seared short beef rib and coral hind from Penghu, bringing the perfect ending to the evening. In the morning, the breakfast contains a bowl of warm vegetable porridge and small dishes made with the ingredients purchased from the local farmers, all with simple seasoning for you to savor the most natural flavors.The name of the villa, ChooArt, is the Taiwanese word for trees, representing a tribute to the land and local hospitality. The team is dedicated to the coexistence of the ecologically sustainable architecture and nature. This dedication also leads ChooArt Villa to be the Gold Winner of the 2017 FIABCI World Prix d’Excellence Environmental Award (as “Oscars Award” of the real estate industry). The team believes that a good balance can be achieved by planting trees while building houses. Just like Brian, the amicable CEO, said: “A lot of things should not be taken for granted, we must learn how to adapt to nature.” His respect for the earth also deeply affects the employees of ChooArt. Working as a staff here, not only one’s capability is a must, but the attitude one bears would be the key. The staff here learn from nature while serving each traveler wholeheartedly.Before you leave, come to the lobby and enjoy some Chinese tea and a good chat with the tea master. With a cup of fine tea, reserve some quiet time for yourself. The aroma drifting in the air just reminds you of the thoughtfulness of ChooArt and the wonderfulness of being embraced by the forest.

Description: Number 36 Lighthouse Home Stay is situated in Hualien City, and is the home stay closest to the ocean. In 1980, Hualien Harbor was extended, and the lighthouse was demolished; a new red lighthouse was later built. The lighthouse during our childhood was a landmark where we gathered and played, and also a place we went to when we are bored. No matter how we played, we and the lighthouse are inseparable. Outside the building, there is an ocean view platform where you can drink coffee leisurely, and enjoy the ocean scenery. Our scenery is worth appreciating and will relax you. Number 36 Lighthouse is the only place with the magnificent sunrise in the east, sea breeze and bright moon at night, sea viewing, wave listening, and the sight  of fishing boats entering and exiting the harbor. Local delicacies, from seafood and bomb scallion pancakes, temple pole black tea, Gong Cheng steamed buns to Yi Hsian won ton can all be eaten nearby. You can also rent motorcycles to travel to each scenic spot. We arrange trips to the famous Nan Bing (Nanbin) and Tzu Chiang (Ziqiang) Night Markets, Bei Bing Park, the beach, Farglory Ocean Park nearby, and also whale watching and river tracing trips.

Description: Yilan｜Shire GuesthouseThe Tranquil Life in a Secluded AlleyOn a balmy afternoon, you set aside your busy life and take a leisurely stroll across the Luodong Sports Park. In the quiet alleys behind the park, among the many rows of residential houses, you see the elegant Chinese characters of the Shire Guesthouse sign. You need not go far to find your ideal lifestyle after all, for it now appears right before your eyes.The leisure to be found within a secluded residenceThe term “Shire” comes from Ｔhe Lord of the Rings and is the place where the Hobbits live. Shire Guesthouse is precisely like the Shire we know from the movies; a warm, leisurely, peaceful life amid the natural beauty of the land. In this place, your hosts Ivan and his wife Ivy have realized their ideal lifestyle. The moment you set foot in Shire Guesthouse, you are greeted by genial sunlight spilling across a soft carpet through large French windows with warm wooden furniture everywhere you look. The design of Shire Guesthouse has a simple beauty which is not showy. The red brick flooring throughout the ground level makes for a cozy living room, extending under the dining table and into the kitchen. The pastiche stone walls stealthily absorb the humidity of the Yilan air, making for ideal temperatures all year round. Even staying indoors, it is easy to find a spot to sit or lounge or flip through a book and enjoy a leisurely time.Ivan, who began learning landscape design when in university, has unique tastes and specialties. He worked with many important construction companies after graduation. The Luodong Sports Park is one of his works of which he is particularly fond. Later on, he fell in love with Ivy, after which time they worked together to realize their aspirations to build a guesthouse. Before retreating into their Shire lifestyle, Ivy who was born in Yilan was working in Taipei as a clothing assistant. Though the bustling city has its charms, Ivy longed to return to her familiar hometown. As such, when Ivan proposed returning to Yilan to open a guesthouse, Ivy threw herself into the project without hesitation in order to create a beautiful life with her lover. A beautiful evening with the BeatlesFollowing the pastiche stone walls upstairs, the unadorned whitewall design evokes the simple life, alleviating your everyday exhaustion. Walking into the shower to wash away your fatigue, the multi-colored porcelain wall tiles add a splash of excitement to life. Continuing the solid-wood theme of the Shire, the bedroom’s wooden pillars were handpicked by Ivan himself. The unpreserved Taiwanese cypress shows the vestiges of time, like the process of the beautification of life itself. In the quiet of the evening, you are accompanied by the Beatles singing “A Hard Day’s Night” as you recline on the retro leather sofa reading a book until the vinyl record clock on the wall points to 11 o’clock. Even nighttime at the Shire is full of vitality. If you are lucky enough, you may have the pleasure of engaging in deep conversation with Ivan and Ivy, which may be the start of a secret adult meeting. Make an appointment on a whim, chatting happily over some drinks from their private red wine collection - tonight you feel just as content as if meeting with intimate friends for the first time in ages. The courage to face your ideal lifeAs the first rays of sunlight spill into the room, you feel prepared to meet a new day. As your footsteps on the stairs signal your descent to the ground floor, Ivy starts to cook a hot breakfast and the delicious aromas fill the air - the Shire menu changes in accordance with the seasons. Yet one thing always stays the same: the courtesy and consideration extended to all travelling guests. The daily menu and ingredients are flexible, so that even the picky traveler can eat their fill. If you haven’t eaten enough, there is no need to feel awkward - Ivy will happily cook another portion for you! “You need a full belly to be able to head out to have fun!” Ivy’s warm, impassioned laugh and your full belly fill you afresh with energy.The appearance of the ideal life may be a little journey with your sisters, a delightful trip with your sweetheart, or perhaps running off bravely on your own adventure. As such, Ivan and Ivy have the consideration to offer a special package for independent travelers, as a way to assist you in setting off on a new life. If it is in your destiny, perhaps Ivy can even accompany you in exploring parts of Yilan you’ve never seen. “In fact, Ivy always says that I’m just like a hobbit, which is why this place is called the Shire.” Ivan smilingly jokes about Ivy. From time to time, the sound of their quarrels and laughter fills the whole house. The Shire feels like a simple, ordinary space, yet it is filled with an indescribable energy that brings warmth and happiness to all who stay there. In this place, the easy atmosphere and genuine ideal lifestyle are shared with you.

Name: Spend Time
Description: Miaoli｜Spend TimeSpend time soaking in hot springs and enjoying nature by the lakesideThe afternoon scenery unfolds before your eyes as you drive up into the mountains in Dahu Township, Miaoli County. There, you find Spend Time guesthouse which melds into the landscape between mountains and lakes, resembling a picturesque painting.Enjoy Mother Nature’s genuine welcomeAs you walk down the stone path from your car to the guesthouse, you are surprised to discover that the main building sits right beside the lake. Water and mountains wrap around on all sides. Vivid flowers and trees abound. You are met by a delicious breeze and dancing butterflies. As you stroll around the wooden guesthouse, you can sense that nature has already prepared a full itinerary for you.Wandering by the flowing brooks on a bright sunny day, you can observe wisteria and sakura flowers in early spring and tung oil tree blossoms toward the end of the season. In the golden autumn, the sycamores turn red and you can behold the starry sky while steeping in hot-spring pools at night. During summer evenings, you open the balcony doors and the fireflies make their debut as the lake shimmers before your eyes. Spend Time guesthouse is always ready to serve you something spectacular whenever you swing by.Beauty in the scenery, the cuisine, the people, and the hot springsAt Spend Time, not only can you enjoy all the beauty that nature unselfishly provides; various kinds of local delicacies and homemade wines are also on offer. The roasted strawberry beer chicken and German-style pig’s trotters are must-try dishes. A Chinese-style breakfast with mouthwatering steamed breads is served lake-side every morning. The housekeeper and all the staff are exceedingly hospitable. You might even have the opportunity to taste unique, homemade grape and kumquat wines.Commonly referred to as “beauty springs”, the sodium bicarbonate hot-springs are one of the distinguishing features here. Spend Time guesthouse insists on providing an authentic hot-spring experience with no extra water or chemical additives whatsoever. Even the bath in your room runs with delicate spring water. The public pools at Spend Time are made from various materials in a number of shapes and sizes, some of them with controllable water temperature, and provide travelers with a uniquely refreshing hot spring experience.Building a dreamlike garden paradiseSpend Time guesthouse is the realization of a common ideal held by two mutually supportive friends. Mr. Lin loves creative work and is captivated by art. Ms. Cai adores working in the kitchen and is also fond of gardening. After a bout of serious illness several years ago, Mr. Lin accelerated his plans to retire and open a guesthouse, inviting Ms. Cai to help him realize his dream. One of the partners took charge of designing the space, and the other took responsibility for the gardens and the creative cuisine. In this way, the seemingly parallel lives of an artist and a housewife came to intersect in the planning and implementation of a beautiful dream.Why not find a day to come “Spend Time” here? Come enjoy this dreamlike garden paradise, relax in the pure, fresh hot spring, savor the gentle surroundings, and delight in the simple pleasures of nature.

Description: At 243 km of Taichung Highway No. 2 (National Freeway No. 3), exit at Jhushan (Zhushan) interchange and turn right towards the direction of Xitou, Lugu (Nantou Highway 151), pass "Chuxiang Bridge," along the mountain road, pass Lugu Towansjip--the home of tea. (At 13 km) there lies a Neihu Elementary School, it has wooden school buildings, which are very rare and worth a visit. Arriving here, it is easy to feel the natural coolness, which is the result of the vast forests. Proceed to (18 km), pass "Moso Bamboo Highway," then you have arrived Xitou. The beauty of Xitou is in the mist, which is cool and pleasant. At the entrance of Xitou Nature Education Park, there is an "Moso Avenue", beside the avenue a "poetry corridor." A "Gigantic Bamboo" of 6 floors high is the world's tallest Dendrocalamus giganteus Munro. Next, go to "Ginkgo Tea Garden,", in the garden you find "Ginkgo Hotel." Xitou is also a special zone for Moso bamboos, Ginkgo Hotel in Chinese is named "Meng Zong", the name after one of 24 filial sons in Chinese history. The Hotel used to be a three-story building, each story is designed for having 24 rooms; therefore a total of 72 rooms. The number of 72 rooms sounds matching the stories of"24 sons of Filial Piety and 72 Virtuous," to shine on the historic events. The business philosophy of Ginkgo Hotel focuses on implementing of "elegant, cordial, and attentive" qualities for creating the most friendly ambience. Ginkgo Hotel is endeavored to keeping 3-star rating quality honor. Xitou is about 1000-1650 meters in elevation and enjoys spectacular views of multitudinous morning sunshine and multifarious evening overcasts. From the sky roof of Ginkgo Hotel, you can overlook Xitou's panoramic view. Guest rooms are decorated with specially produced Moso bamboos providing charcoal air purification, and other charcoal supplies, which obtain a high satisfaction rating. For 40 years, Ginkgo Hotel has served over one million visitors, scholars Yafang specially selected Mr. Zhang Daxiu's poems of Xitou, hired calligraphers Mr. Chen Lianzhong to write the poems on ancient cypress boards for exhibitions, sharing the masterpieces of cultural and creative productions with staying tourists. After the 921 earthquake reconstruction, each floor is designed to have 18 rooms, and the building has 4 stories; therefore, it has a total of 72 rooms. We prepare foods with local flavors and support the concepts of maintaining good health, diligently keeping our star-rated quality, and launching new services. Ginkgo coffee, fun of making tea, listening Xitou story. "Bamboo grilled rice" and "rice with dried bamboo shoots fast food" are innovative. Xitou is a suitable place for enjoying your vacation, fitness activities, nourishing the mind and body, temporary stay, and relaxing life. Colleagues of Ginkgo Hotel would be happy to provide you depth interpretation services, accompany you strolling in the mysterious forests of Xitou, elegantly experiencing the beauty of Xitou and the quality of Ginkgo Hotel services.

Name: Live Guesthouse
Description: Kinmen｜Live GuesthouseEasy listening every day at Kinmen Live GuesthouseAfter a flight across a stretch of ocean, you follow your map into the alleys and laneways of Kinmen. In contrast to the other large settlements in Kinmen, Oucuo Village is a simple, tranquil place, allowing you the time and space for romantic wandering. Turning down that unassuming little road, the sea breeze carries the sound of a guitar to your ear. Lively and spontaneous, the melody carries you into the daily life at Live Guesthouse.Blank space for your imagination to unfoldLow walls constructed of irregularly sized bricks with old, darkly colored wooden doors open inwards to a courtyard decorated with a few large potted trees. The faded paint of the old wooden chairs create a pleasant vacation atmosphere. The main hall connected to the courtyard serves as a common living room for travelling guests. The simple furnishings add luster to the old building. An artistic painting and two acoustic guitars hung high on the walls speak about the daily lives of the hosts. The afternoon sun slants into the enclosed courtyard of this traditional Minnan house, while clothing hung high in the breeze to dry sways as if to the rhythm of the Live Guesthouse beat. “Why not come this way, your room is over here.” The male half of your couple of hosts, Xu-Ran, is from Beijing. With his special accent and style of speaking, he leads you inside with a smile. Live Guesthouse has one double room, and two loft-style four-person rooms. The small room is perfect for visiting with a friend or to enjoy the the freedom of travelling alone. The interior paint appears new and original - a large swath of white wall intersected by a stripe of aquamarine creates just the right contrast with the other red brick floor, creating an atmosphere of harmony and vitality. In your room, there is a poem in simplified Chinese, and a different poem, expressing the emotions of Chinese poets, has been left in each room, corresponding with the customs and style of Kinmen. The charm implicit in the poem’s simplicity corresponds precisely to the impression that hosts Xu-Ran and Wang-Ling leave you with.A guitar’s melody like a slow, dreamy eveningLive Guesthouse invites you to arrive without a plan. Wang-Ling and her older sister established “Local Methodology”, providing an ideal opportunity for exploration. Even a short conversation with Wang-Ling opens the cultural landscape of Kinmen up before you. Even though she has married, she chooses to remain in Kinmen to follow her dreams. Fortunately, her husband Xu-Ran also prefers the pace of Kinmen to the big city of Beijing. As such, he was willing to pack a bag, grab his guitar and follow his wife back to Kinmen to put down roots. Some afternoon, you may also get the chance to explore Xu-Ran’s secret music collection with him. He is himself a guitarist who performs in the band Momo Sky, and has insisted that each room be equipped with a CD player so that he can share his collection with travelers. Perusing the lyrics in the CD booklet, you feel a warmth lacking in today’s online music world. It matches beautifully with the slow rhythm of life in Kinmen.Other than compact disk music, if you are lucky, you may get to see a live performance, acoustic guitar music lingering in the courtyard. Xu-Ran’s focused and easy music merges into the old courtyard home. You might take a book and sit quietly on the sofa, or grab another guitar and play in harmony. In this sunset composition, you smile as you strum one final chord and the sound echoes leisurely into the night and into your dreams. Stroll along the beach and explore Kinmen daily cultureEarly in the morning, before the town has really woken up, the music from the night before still echoes in your ears. Your step is particularly light after a sound night’s sleep, you carry the light snacks prepared by Live Guesthouse down towards the beach. Less than ten minutes from the guesthouse, you can see Oucuo Beach, where people, searching the island for traces of war, come to marvel at the scenery a tank stranded in the sand. Description: A story: a young child, playing under the apple tree, said goodbye to parents in the brisk and set off to find the legendary treasure of happiness. Standing on the grass in front of the house, the air is extremely clean, the owner Wenxuan said: "To the right is my son's school, 12 people a class, to the left is my prayer chapel, in front of me, the organic rice field I am working on, followed by a .... Hostess Su Qing described the impact of life-turning process.  "I have no way to get rid of the genetic bones of creative desires." Wenxuan, an Information Engineer, and his father is an average-people turned sculptor, but he found his creative outlet on his wife's interior design field. In order to have a place for creating sculptures, he started to arrange a studio; however, the arrangement lasted for two years, because of his haunting perfect aesthetic perception.  Children grew up, the house was finally completed at the beginning of the year, and then looking back, the journey has already lasted for six years. Originally, it was a decision made without hesitation to put down everything in the city, though I lost something, all is worth it, because what I have now are impossible, even devoting whole life, to get from a city, rustic life, paddy waves, rice fragrance, noise of children's frolic, and the hometown mien, which I believe are luxurious hopes.  I often also think that it was lucky for people of our generation have a chance to return, look at the children, and think of myself, what I am worried about is that how to pave a smooth home returning way for the kids and let them know that there is a way back home they should remember, and the parents at the home will always light up a lamp waiting for them.

Name: Pearl Homestay (Tese Homestay)
Description: Slow down the pace. Listen to the sound of your heart. Enjoy the nature and the country life. Pearl Homestay is in Shanhou Folk Culture Village, Kinmen. Shanhou Folk Culture Village consists of 18 Minnan style old houses built during the Qing Dynasty. The construction lasted for 25 years to build the finest houses. To this day, the old houses remain the same as they were first built. The traditionally living space is well presented. Shanhou Folk Culture Village sits on the back of Shishan, facing Dongge Bay. Every morning when the sun rises up from the horizon, the sun shines into the halls. What's more Shanhou village used to be a restricted military base. Thus the environment of Wuhu Mountain is well preserved. There is a trail up just outside the village. There are also wetlands nearby where you can see native plants and insects. The abandoned military base, the intertidal zone are within walking distance. Traveling by bike is also a good way to go around. There are mountains and the sea around the homestay. You don't have to travel far to see and feel the nature. Slow down the pace and feel the tranquility. Enjoy the view of the moon and the stars. All the hustle and bustle of the city are miles away. Enjoy the nature, the fresh air and the lovely plants. When you stay at Pearl Homestay, look up to the sky and you will see clouds, birds, and butterflies. And there are organic vegetables that I grown myself for breakfast. Kinmen souvenirs available for free.
Add: No.65, Shanhou, Jinsha Township, Kinmen County 890, Taiwan (R.O.C.)

Name: SPRING HILL RESORT
Description: Located in the northern foothills of Mt. Dagang and with natural cold springs, Spring Hill Resort is an oasis from the rat race for the body, mind, and soul. Sitting on over 23,000 square meters of land, it is focused three themes: health, art, and culture. We pride ourselves on our promotion of cold-springs tourism, along with flower-filled walking trails, karaoke, a study, a children’s room, nude bathing pools,and springs cabins, . The hotel is focused on promoting a slower pace of life, and the pools, whether private ones in the rooms or large public ones, offer natural, nourishing springs bathing. In terms of dining, our Chinese-style meals use seasonal ingredients sourced from the surrounding Tainan, Alian, and Tianliao areas, prepared by our creative chefs. We also offer elegant Chinese-style set meals and Western food including handmade Italian food, along with high-quality teas, coffees, and fruit juices to help you while away a relaxing afternoon. The main dining hall can accommodate 110 people and our conference room is of the highest quality, providing all the necessities, along with snacks that can be tailored to your conference’s needs. Our 30 high-class guest rooms average around 50 square meters, and include private baths and dry/wet segregated bathroom areas, offering a perfect mix of springs bathing and spectacular scenery. Additionally, we are near well-known tourist destinations like “Moon World,” the three-century-old Chaofeng Temple, Erliao (a great place to catch the sunrise), Chaoyuan Temple, and Qishan Old Street, providing a wonderful travel experience for guests of all ages.

Name: Song He Xiang He Ju Homestay
Description: Songhe B&B is located along the scenic and wide Taose Highway in Gongguan Township, Miaoli County. It's next to Ren'an Community Center along Mountain Road, with Tianquan Temple nearby. Behind the B&B are lush green mountains, hiking trail and Exercise Park. A hike up the mountain offers a birds-eye-view of Gongguan Township and the beautiful night scene of the entire Gongguan Town. This area is surrounded by greenery and flowers, sounds of birds chirping, insects buzzing, butterflies fluttering about and fireflies flickering at night. The soothing sounds of water running in the farm field ditches and fish swimming in the pond remind visitors from the busy city of the carefree country lifestyle and childhood games, such as catching grasshoppers and fishing for loach.                      Nearby attractions in the southern part of Miaoli include Miaoli Hakka Mansion, Hakka Cultural Museum, Shengxing Station, Tenglong Bridge Ruins, Taiwan Oil Field Exhibition Hall, Miaoli Pottery Museum, Da Hu Wineland Resort, Wenshui Old Street, Qing'an Tofu Street, Tai'an Hot Spring Area, Wugu Cutural Village, Westlake Village Resortopia, Sanyi Wood Sculpture Museum and Sanyi Wood Sculpture Street. Scenic attractions in the northern part of Miaoli are Shitan Xiancao Street, Mt. Xianshan, Nanzhuang Old Street and Mt. Shitou. Seeing is believing. All of us at Songhe B&B welcome you to Miaoli to enjoy the beautiful scenery.

Description: The building compound is located outside Dashe, Zhushan, and is a traditional-style structure with an impressive layout. The outside is covered with six-sided bricks, an example of rare Kinmen craftsmanship. Welcome to Zhushan No. 41 Bed & Breakfast, where you can take a break to appreciate the beauty of this old building. We hope each visitor is a precious contribution to the development of Kinmen.

Description: In the announcement, I've told everyone that the B&B is simple and unadorned. There is no high class furniture and decoration, no luxurious facilities and no professional services. You may have questions. What does the selling point of my B&B? I will tell you the answer. I sell the scenery of Penghu to you. I had not been to Shili in a long while.  Every time when I thought of it, I would burst into tears. When I was a kid, the road of Shili was next to the beach, and the sea and the sky were of one hue. The fishing sampans were hauled on the beach, and I stood on the beach, feeling that it was a merging space, like what it said in the Disney cartoon Atlantis: The Lost Empire, "It is part of it, while it is also a part of it." But now, the huge sea walls and overweight tetrapods have occupied the coast, crushed the memory of childhood and broken off the dialogue with nature. The coast is disappearing. Now, I look at the tide water rising and ebbing and the shadow changing on the sea surface from the glass window in the house, and I haven't done this for a long time. The people who visit here always praise that I am clear-eyed. What chance would it be for me to find such a nice place? When it comes to this question, I feel distressed about it. Sadly, I have to tell you that there were other places and coasts more beautiful than here in Penghu. But what have we done to the beautiful islands? People keep constructing buildings and ignore the destruction of ecological environment. If you feel touched when staying here, please love the land you live on. So I often sell my B&B with the sad irony of, "the more destruction in Penghu, the higher the value of my place." Chengqian, a small village. Thanks to being small and without large budgets, few destructing construction appears in Chengqian, which forms part of the natural coastline and the rich ecology of an intertidal zone. You can see prosperous Magong City on the other side, the tortuous islands of Xiyu Township and the precious location of the inner sea, Dacang village. The blue sea and sky of the day and the glittering stars of the night present the original sea viewing of Penghu. We hope you will like it.

Name: Moon Lake House Inn
Description: We are the legal house inn No.63 in Taichung city. Moon Lake House Inn,, Introduction Xinshe is the largest fluvial terraces in Taiwan. Ten thousand years ago, the activities of human beings had already existed here, and a century ago Bai-Len Canal was constructed here, a considerable feat of irrigation works at the time. The climate is cool and comfortable, and the best breeds of mushrooms, loquat, grapes, and Oncidium grow here; pleasant scenery, convenient transportation, floral festivals year after year, and attractions everywhere, here is the Yangmingshan in Taichung. Mon Lake House Inn, B&B, is located on the side of Moon Lake Fluvial Terrace, facing Dongshih on the opposite side of Dajia River, having vast horizons, extending peaks of Mt. Hengling, Mt. Yuanzui, Mt. Shaolai, Mt. Xiaoxue are presenting in front of you. In the night, bugs chirp and frogs chant, and Taiwan No. 8 Line looks like Galaxy with lights on. It is hard to imagine that here is just one km from Xinshe downtown, and we have the convenience of a city and the tranquility of rural life. Your host and hostess are born gardeners, crazy lovers of flowers, both personally planted the flowers and trees, which all are nearly 30 years old; the original appearance of the house has been kept for more than forty years. Decorations come from family and friends, including Papa's wind drum of more than 60 years old, Mom's dowry table and ancient shoulder pole for selling vegetables, younger sister's trophies of exploring the world, my son's paintings, and my daughter's drawing cards, etc., A little bit here and a little bit there are all our intentions to make you feel the warmth. The old house is the most mini here. We have only three rooms that can accommodate up to 8 people. Wireless Internet services. If you are interested in plants, you are welcomed to visit our secret garden. We advocate the concept of "Leave No Trace" and environmental protection activities of health and low-carbon; therefore, we hope the visitors bring their own personal toiletries,ex: towels, toothbrushes, and razors,etc. We welcome your family or friends together to appreciate the natural and cultural beauties of Xinshe, and enjoy the quiet simple happiness of our little home.

Description: Le Méridien Hotels, renowned worldwide for their deep connection to culture and art, trace their origins to the fashion capital—Paris. With a forward-thinking and trendsetting essence, Le Méridien not only provides guests with a flawless stay but also offers an inspiring journey of effortless exploration.Officially opened on December 3, 2010, Le Méridien Taipei is located in the heart of Taipei’s fashion and arts district—Xinyi. Rooted in the curatorial concept of contemporary art, the hotel embraces the theme of "light and shadow," seamlessly integrating art into every corner accessible to guests. This non-traditional approach fosters direct interaction between guests and artistic expression, transforming the hotel into a dynamic gallery space. The curated collection features nearly 700 works and installations by contemporary artists from Taiwan, China, Japan, Korea, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Belgium, spanning various mediums and forms. Through these visionary artworks, guests are invited to engage their senses and ignite their creative thinking.Designed with a modern and minimalist architectural aesthetic, the hotel meticulously crafts 160 guestrooms and suites, offering six distinct room types with lofty ceilings. Each room is thoughtfully furnished with the Sealy bed, a 60-inch flat-screen TV, an immersive surround sound system, high-speed internet, a multimedia hub, and an illy espresso machine, creating a seamless blend of comfort and functionality for both work and relaxation.The bathroom design exudes refined sophistication, featuring a rainforest shower, a bidet toilet, and premium large-sized amenities from the American brand MALIN+GOETZ, harmonizing sustainability with luxury. Additionally, most room types include an independent bathtub, set within a spacious and elegantly designed bathroom, offering an indulgent and immersive bathing experience—transforming each stay into an unforgettable journey of refined comfort.Le Méridien Taipei brings together a diverse array of dining experiences, crafted with meticulous attention to detail to offer the ultimate gastronomic indulgence. My Humble House Restaurant showcases the exquisite artistry of classic Cantonese cuisine, presenting refined and masterfully prepared gourmet delights. Latest Recipe curates global delicacies, offering freshly made-to-order creative dishes that captivate the palate with boundless surprises. Meanwhile, Latitude 25 Lobby Bar harmonizes the cultural essence of illy® coffee with an exclusive selection of fine wines coveted by connoisseurs worldwide, creating an unparalleled ambiance for relaxation and refinement.In 2024, the hotel unveiled two new in-house dining concepts. Drip & Dough offers a tranquil ambiance with warm wooden tones and a contemporary artistic flair, featuring hand-brewed coffee from Cupping Room, a Hong Kong-based champion roastery, paired with exquisite pastries and light bites—inviting travelers to immerse themselves in a leisurely, sensory journey. TIPSY Sparrow, a collaboration between a Michelin-starred chef and an award-winning mixologist, reinterprets classic cuisine through a modern lens, creating a social dining experience inspired by French and American flavors. The bar also introduces an exclusive selection of cocktails infused with the rich essence of Taiwanese tea, delivering a uniquely sophisticated and innovative tasting experience.
